### M18 · Worktree runtime decisions
- D-2440: M18 is a new milestone section owning F-WT-06 (and F-WT-09), P2 like M17's; `check-coverage.sh` allows P2 in M18. The work lands on `competitive-gaps`, the branch this session is pinned to, fast-forwarded to `chain19`.
- D-2441: The runtime is on only when the file has `ports` or `env`; without them nothing changes for existing worktrees (no surprise `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`).
- D-2442: `env` is trusted with the commands (a repository could otherwise set variables that run code in every shell). The digest adds `env` only when there is some, so trust given under F-WT-01 stays valid; ports need no trust. Names that change how shells start (`PATH`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `BASH_ENV`, `PROMPT_COMMAND`, `ZDOTDIR`…), and Vibezeo's own, are refused outright, trusted or not.
- D-2443: Blocks come from 41000–48999, first fit, never overlapping any worktree on the computer, checked by binding 127.0.0.1 at creation; kept in a JSON file in the data folder rather than a migration (no schema change other branches would meet). A file that gains or changes `ports` after a worktree was made reassigns it on its next pane.
- D-2444: `<slug>.localhost` is used only where this computer resolves it to loopback (checked once per run), because the built-in browser on Linux uses the system resolver; otherwise `localhost`.
- D-2446: A preview is "ready" when a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1 on its port succeeds within 250 ms; no request is sent, so a server that needs a path or auth still counts as up. The rail polls only while it's open and the window visible, at most 64 worktrees a call.
- D-2447: A new worktree runs setup and preview in one pane (`<setup> && <preview>`) so the preview never starts before dependencies are installed; with no setup the preview gets its own "Preview" pane. Best of N lanes (made by the core) start previews only from Compare's Previews.
- D-2448 (review of F-WT-06): a worktree's variables went into a pane after the launch environment, so a trusted file could replace an engine pane's provider home (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_*_HOME`) or point its requests elsewhere. Now `layer_pane_env` applies them under the launch's (provider home, hook token and engine variables win), and `reserved_reason` refuses provider homes, `*_BASE_URL`, proxies and certificate overrides in any case, saying why; a test checks every registry `providerHomeEnv` is reserved. API keys stay allowed.
- D-2449: Clones use the `FICLONE` ioctl directly (what `cp --reflink=auto` does) rather than shelling out to `cp`, behind the `Cloner` trait; any failure to clone falls back to `std::fs::copy`, never to an error, and the destination is created exclusively so nothing is overwritten. The real-filesystem test runs only where `TANDEM_COW_DIR` points at a reflink-capable folder (CI's tmpfs and overlayfs can't clone).
- D-2450: Side by side is built in the UI from existing commands (`tab_create`, `pane_create` with a URL, `pane_rename`, `tab_rename`) rather than a new IPC; the panes go into the layout before the tab is shown, as `moveToNewTab` does. Pane names keep their 1–32-character, unique-per-workspace rule: a long branch is shortened with "…" and a taken name gets " 2"…" 5"; failing that the pane keeps its page title. It waits up to 60 s for both previews, polling every 2 s, then says they didn't answer.
- D-2451: F-WT-07 and F-WT-08 get their own M18 section ("merge and CI"). The base is the repository's current branch, and the candidates are its local worktrees with commits it doesn't have; SSH and WSL folders can't land (their git runs elsewhere).
- D-2452: Each worktree takes the base by a merge, not a rebase, so its branch history stays as the agent left it and the check runs on exactly what lands. That merge stays in the worktree after Undo landing. Every merge the queue starts is aborted on a conflict, so a stopped queue never leaves a merge in progress.
- D-2453: The check command is typed in UI-155 and remembered per repository in `$DATA/landing.json`, not read from `.vibezeo/worktree.json`: it runs only when a person starts the landing from the main window, so it needs no trust digest. Its limit is 30 minutes (a full test suite), against Best of N's 10.
- D-2454: Undo landing is `git reset --keep` to the recorded commit, allowed only while the base's HEAD is the last landed merge and no landed merge is in `origin/<base>`; like Discard it needs the main window and the native confirm. The record survives relaunch; a new landing replaces it.
- D-2455: A running landing lives in memory and UI-155 reads it every second (no event), as the rail reads previews.
- D-2456: F-WT-08 reads GitHub only through the user's `gh` (no API client, no token in Vibezeo), so it works wherever the user has signed `gh` in. The allow is per repository (any of its worktrees asks for it) and kept on this computer; reading checks never sends anything to an agent.
- D-2457: GitLab's checks aren't read in this slice: `glab`'s JSON output for pipelines couldn't be checked here, and true claims come first. GitLab worktrees say so.
- D-2458: An imported review comment keeps the reviewer's words for display, but the review prompt carries the core's fenced copy (`fenced`), built with `tandem_core::untrusted`, so the TypeScript side never assembles untrusted text into a prompt itself.
- D-2520: Review of F-WT-07 (B1). Undo landing requires the base's first-parent history since the recorded commit to be exactly the landed merges (`rev-list --first-parent`), so a commit made under or after the landing is never reset away. Pushed means any remote-tracking branch contains the first landed merge (`for-each-ref --contains`), not just `origin/<base>`.
- D-2521: Each step merges a pinned commit, not a branch name: step 1 merges the base's expected commit (`--ff`, whatever `merge.ff` says) and notes the worktree's result; step 3 lands that noted commit as "Merge branch '<branch>'". Before each step the base must be on its branch at the expected commit, and before step 3 the worktree must be on its branch at the noted commit with no tracked changes, else the queue stops ("moved during the landing", "changed during its check").
- D-2522: A merge that would add a path already on disk but not in that checkout's HEAD is refused before it starts (`diff --diff-filter=A --no-renames HEAD <rev>`): git overwrites ignored files in a true merge, and Undo's `reset --keep` would then delete them. Revisions follow `--end-of-options` (git 2.24), except `reset`, which takes only a recorded commit id.
- D-2523: Stop is a sticky cancel on the check's slot (`bestof::CheckSlot`), shared with Best of N: cancelled before the spawn the check never starts, right after it's killed once registered, and the queue checks it before steps 2 and 3. The tree kill is `kill -KILL -<pgid>` on Unix and `taskkill /T /F /PID` on Windows behind `TreeKiller`. A check's output keeps its last 64 KiB as it streams.
- D-2524: Quitting calls `merge_queue::shutdown()` from the Exit handler. The merge a run is in is recorded in `landing.json` while it runs; the next plan or start for that repository aborts a leftover merge only when `MERGE_HEAD` is that recorded commit, and UI-155 says so. Starts reserve the repository under one lock. A run's first landing replaces the undo record; a run that lands nothing keeps the previous one.
- D-2525: Review of F-WT-08. Polls skip while one runs and read only worktrees whose checks are running, unread or errored; the rest every 15 minutes or on Refresh. CI logs are stripped of terminal escapes, kept to 200 lines and 16 KiB, and an unreadable log says why. Imports skip outdated comments (`line` null), bring at most 40 of 2,000 characters each and say what they left out, and remember imported ids per worktree so sent or removed comments don't return. An imported comment's file and line are inside its fence, and it can't be edited.
- D-2527: Re-review of e0e1d806. `lane_review_comments` takes the ids the worktree imported before and drops them before the 40-comment cap, so 45 comments arrive as 40 then 5. `start` recovers a merge left by a quit before anything else (its reservation stands for the "no run here" check). A landing git reports as already up to date lands nothing: no undo record, and UI-155 says "Already in {base}". CI log tails are redacted whole, then cut to 16 KiB.
- D-2528: F-WT-10 parses with tree-sitter (0.25, with the TypeScript/TSX 0.23, Rust 0.24 and Python 0.25 grammars), an addition to DECISIONS' Rust stack. It lives in `tandem_git::symbols`, not a new crate, since the layout is fixed; the grammars are C compiled by `cc` at build time, and the gate's windows-check (MinGW) and macos-check (both Mac architectures) build them. Size: a stripped Linux x86-64 release binary linking the four grammars and tree-sitter is 4.94 MB against 0.34 MB without, so about 4.6 MB, almost all the grammars' parse tables.
- D-2529: The radar compares bare names: definitions are keyed by qualified name within a file, but two worktrees share a symbol when the bare name matches (a use is just an identifier on an added line). To keep that from flooding, only changed-or-removed definitions count, names under 3 characters are ignored, and a definition one side only added is never reported. A rename shows as removed + added, which is what catches "renamed here, used there".
- D-2530: Indexes live in memory with a per-file parse cache keyed by each changed file's content, so a refresh after a checkpoint parses only the files whose content changed since the last refresh (those the turn touched) and reuses the rest; reading and parsing run on the blocking pool (`spawn_blocking`), never on the async runtime's threads or the UI. Refreshed per worktree on `checkpoint:created` (the radar listener) and by `lane_overlap`; `lane_radar` only reads them. A pair's notice is keyed by the pair and its symbol list, so a checkpoint that changes nothing in the overlap doesn't repeat it. Warn both agents follows F-WT-08's rule: the core builds each note (names and branches behind the untrusted fence), and the UI types it only on the click.
- D-2531: F-CD-22 finds a multi-repo folder by looking, not by setting: a local folder outside any repository whose direct, non-hidden subfolders include at least two with `.git` (up to 12). `WorkspaceSummary.repos` carries their names (optional in TypeScript, so nothing else changes). Nested repositories and submodules aren't looked for.
- D-2532: A multi-repo worktree keeps one `workspaces` row, the parent folder `<folder>/.tandem/worktrees/<slug>` (`lane_base` empty), and a `lane_repos` row per repository (migration 0004) with its own base. `LaneManager::create_multi` picks one slug free in every repository and the folder, and rolls back everything it made (worktrees, branches, folder) if any repository fails, naming it.
- D-2533: The gate is a new `Limits.multiRepo` (Free off, Pro and Team on), `#[serde(default)]` so an older API's entitlement still parses; `lanes::create` takes the limits, and refuses with ForbiddenPlan before touching disk. Superseded by D-869 (Vibezeo is free): the limit and the check are gone, and multi-repo worktrees are free for everyone.
- D-2534: Features that need one repository (merge, overlap, Create pull request, the radar, landing, checks, previews, setup, second opinion) refuse a multi-repo worktree with "Not available for multi-repo worktrees yet", or skip it; the menu disables them under a note. Diff prefixes each path with the repository's name, so F-WT-02's comments and prompt work unchanged. Discard uses one confirmation for every repository (`LaneManager::remove_many`; `ForceConfirm` stays uncopyable), and without force refuses files left in the parent folder outside the repositories.
- D-2535: Create pull requests runs in the core, not typed into a shell: per repository with commits past its base, `git push -u origin tandem/<slug>` (the app's git) and `gh pr create --fill --head` (the user's `gh`, F-WT-08's runner), then `gh pr view`/`gh pr edit --body-file` append "Related pull requests". It's behind the native confirm from the main window; one repository failing doesn't stop the others; GitLab remotes are skipped this slice.
- D-2581: Review of ed496574 (F-CD-22). Multi-repo worktrees and folders are refused up front by one guard, `lanes::single_repo` (a worktree with `lane_repos` rows, or a local top-level folder that detection calls multi-repo), in setup, landing, pull request checks, previews and second opinion; `lane_setup` answers null and the radar skips them, so nothing fails halfway or shows "Worktrees need a git repository".
- D-2582: Detection groups a folder's checkouts by their git common directory, so a repository and its own worktree beside it are one repository (the first name sorted). Over 12 repositories the folder isn't multi-repo at all (rather than the first 12), and `WorkspaceSummary.reposNote` says why in the row's tooltip.
- D-2583: Creating a multi-repo worktree takes its parent folder with `create_dir` (exclusive) and retries the next slug on a collision; a rollback force-removes the worktrees it made, prunes and deletes the new branches, the failing repository's included, logging what it couldn't undo. The workspace row and its `lane_repos` rows are one transaction; a revived row drops old repositories; Discard clears them, since removal is a soft update and the cascade never runs.
- D-2584: Create pull requests: a push has 5 minutes; a repository whose branch already has an open pull request (a re-run) keeps it instead of failing; the description is read before it's edited and left alone if it can't be; the links are appended once; the description file is a fresh `create_new` file in `$DATA/run`, removed after `gh pr edit`.
- D-2585: A worktree made from a multi-repo worktree (a handoff) starts each repository from that worktree's HEAD, while `repo_root` stays the repository's own checkout. Multi-repo patches carry the repository's name in their `diff --git`, `---`/`+++` and rename headers, as the file paths do.
- D-2526: Resolved review threads are still imported: GitHub's REST API doesn't expose resolution, and GraphQL (which does) couldn't be checked from this session. Left for a later slice with a fake-`gh` test of the GraphQL shape.
- D-2536: F-CD-23 talks to language servers itself (a small JSON-RPC client in `services::lsp`) rather than through a crate: it needs only initialize, full-text sync, definition, references, hover and pushed diagnostics, and the client answers the server's own requests (`workspace/configuration` with nulls, the rest with null) so servers that ask don't stall. Positions stay 0-based lines and UTF-16 characters end to end, which is what both LSP and CodeMirror count.
- D-2537: The editor's full text is sent on every sync (`textDocumentSync` 1, debounced 500 ms, the first at once), as `didOpen` then `didChange` with a version (nothing when the text is what the server has); after sending, `lsp_sync` waits up to 1.5 s for the server's next diagnostics for the file. Incremental sync isn't worth its bookkeeping at editor file sizes. Servers are keyed by folder and program; a file under `.tandem/worktrees/<slug>/` opened from the repository gets the worktree's own server, so a worktree's types come from its own files.
- D-2538: Starts are gated per folder and server, not under the map's lock, so a slow rust-analyzer start never holds up a Python request; the least recently used server stops when a fifth starts. A failed start or a crash counts toward 3 in 10 minutes, after which the status line says "{server} stopped: …" until the window passes. Servers run with the login environment like engines (`env_clear` plus the login variables), stderr discarded, and `kill_on_drop`; on Windows without a console window.
- D-2539: Without a server, go to definition falls back to F-WT-10's tree-sitter index for the same file (Rust, TypeScript, Python), and folders on SSH hosts and in WSL use only that fallback in this slice. The diff's name menu reads the new side's text from disk (the worktree's file) and opens the result in the Files tab's context when the worktree is inside it, else its own.
- D-2580: Review of 0ff6251c (coordinator): language servers start only for a repository trusted for language servers, kept in `$DATA/lsp-trust.json` by its main checkout (so its worktrees share it) and given by `lsp_trust` from the main window after the native confirm. A safe mode wasn't enough: `cargo metadata` follows a repository's `.cargo/config.toml` (`build.rustc`, wrappers) and `rust-toolchain.toml` makes rustup download, typescript-language-server prefers the repository's own `node_modules/typescript`, and gopls may switch toolchains. Pyright runs a Python interpreter to find its search paths, and a repository's config can steer which, so it waits too: one rule for every server. An installed server that waits says "{server} is off until you trust this repository" (`LspState::Untrusted`) with Trust repository…; one that isn't installed still says it's missing. Go to definition uses the same-file fallback meanwhile. The trust is separate from Worktree setup's, which trusts a digest of commands, not the repository's code.
- D-2586: Review of 0ff6251c (F-CD-23), trust. With the F-TL-11 sandbox on, a worktree isn't covered by its repository's trust: its own folder is the trust key and the confirm warns that the agent's code will run outside its sandbox (`LspDocument.sandboxed`, "Trust worktree…"). Servers run with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` and from `$DATA/lsp` (npm's `.cmd` shims look for `node` in the current folder first), the workspace reaching them through `rootUri` and `workspaceFolders`; the docs no longer say everything stays local, since a trusted server may fetch declared dependencies.
- D-2587: Servers stop inside `lanes::remove_with_teardown`, after the worktree's panes stop and before the folder is deleted, for every caller (Discard, Best of N, the task host): open handles block `git worktree remove` on Windows, and cargo check would recreate `target/` in a deleted folder.
- D-2588: The client reads frames with header lines capped at 1 KiB and 32 headers, bodies at 8 MiB (larger ones are read past and skipped); a body that doesn't parse is retried with surrogate escapes replaced by U+FFFD, else skipped, so a JavaScript server's lone surrogate never ends a live server. Writes go through one task with a 10 s limit per message and a 256-message queue (full means stuck); server requests are answered without waiting on it, the document map is never held across an await, a timed-out request sends `$/cancelRequest`, and `stop` gives up politely after 4 s and kills the process group (`kill -KILL -<pgid>`, `taskkill /T /F`). Servers are found and started through `flatpak-spawn --host` in a Flatpak, and the last stderr line goes into "stopped: …". Errors are a `ClientError` enum.
- D-2589: rust-analyzer counts as installed only when `rust-analyzer --version` succeeds (rustup's proxy without the component fails it), cached for a minute per PATH. The reaper records a dead server as a failure, so a crash loop reaches the 3-in-10-minutes limit; idle and dead servers stop outside the map's lock.
- D-2590: The editor tells servers about closed tabs (`lsp_close`, `didClose`) and the Files watcher's batches (`lsp_files_changed`, `didChangeWatchedFiles`). Diagnostics are kept by the file's parsed path, not the URI string. Location previews read each file once, at most 2 MiB, in `spawn_blocking`. A path outside the folder (a dependency opened from a definition) gets "Outside this folder: read only, without code intelligence" rather than an error. UI requests wait 45 s (a first request may start the server), trust 10 minutes. Diff names are buttons, so the keyboard reaches them.
- D-2591: Verification review of 0ff6251c..c0e86030. A discarded worktree's own trust is forgotten with its servers, inside `remove_with_teardown` (`lsp::forget_worktree`, `untrust`), since slugs and rows at the same folder are reused. A worktree is recognised by Vibezeo's layout (`<owner>/.tandem/worktrees/<slug>`) as well as by git, so a multi-repo worktree gets the sandbox rule, and without the sandbox its folder's trust covers it. Turning the sandbox setting on stops every server, so ones started under a repository's trust start again only past the new check. The trust check runs whether or not the server is installed, so one installed between two requests never starts untrusted.
- D-2592: A server found dead is taken out and stopped (its tree killed) outside the lock, and counted. `stop` kills the tree while the server still holds its pid (Windows can't reuse it), then the server; on Unix the group is killed afterwards too, for children that outlive their leader; `taskkill` runs without a console window. Quitting stops every server at once within 7 s. A folder being removed gets no new server for 30 s, and a folder that's gone gets none.
- D-2593: typescript-language-server starts with `disableAutomaticTypingAcquisition`, so tsserver never npm-installs type packages the project didn't declare. Smaller fixes: the notification is registered before the diagnostics check, the blank line isn't counted as a header, a verbatim `\\?\` path is simplified in URIs on Windows, the worktree prefix is matched by path components, and the probe runs in `spawn_blocking`.
- D-2594: A worktree's trust is cleared when a worktree is made at its path (`lanes::create` and `create_multi` call `lsp::untrust_new_worktree`), so a trust left behind when its row went with its workspace, or its folder was deleted outside the app, never reaches the next one. Discard still forgets it. The trust store's data folder is reachable in tests (`lsp::data_dir`, one shared temporary folder, since trust is keyed by path), and both removal paths are tested through `lanes::remove` and workspace removal.
- D-2595: A server that is still starting isn't kept if its folder was forgotten or is being removed, or every server stopped (quit, sandbox switch), meanwhile: `client` reads a generation and a forget counter before it checks, and checks again under the map's lock before inserting; a superseded server is stopped. Removal holds a `Closing` guard (`begin_removal`, `forget_worktree`) for as long as it runs, so no server starts during a long teardown, instead of a 30 s timer. `lsp_files_changed` only feeds servers of trusted folders. Every key and comparison goes through one normaliser (`dunce::simplified`), so Windows' verbatim and plain spellings match.
- D-2596: With the agent sandbox on, the main checkout's trust confirm and the docs say that language servers run outside the sandbox, so code agents write in the repository's own folder can run outside it once trusted (the minimum; a lapse on build-file edits is left for later). Smaller fixes: `worktree_of` takes only a plain slug and refuses `..` after it; on Unix the process group is killed before the leader is reaped, and ids of 1 or less are never signalled; a UNC path's URI is `file://host/share/…`; `Spawned::on_stop` lets test fakes record stops.
- D-2597: Round 4 of F-CD-23's review. The command layer takes the servers' epoch (generation and forget count) before it reads the sandbox setting and decides trust, and runs the request with it (`lsp::with_epoch`, a task-local); `client` checks it right after taking the folder's start gate and again before keeping a new server, so a request let through before a sandbox switch (or a forget) never starts one after it, and says "Language servers restarted: the sandbox setting changed". `begin_removal` makes its guard as the closing count goes up; `Closing` and `forget_worktree` are `#[must_use]`. Removing a workspace holds the same guard while it runs and forgets its worktrees' trust (`.tandem/worktrees`), so a folder made there again by hand asks again. `lsp_files_changed` skips folders without a running server before reading trust.
- D-2598: F-CD-24 lanes are jj workspaces only in repositories co-located with git (`.jj` beside `.git`): git keeps the repository, so its exclude file keeps `.tandem/` out of jj's working copy, and the base commit and the other worktrees stay readable. A jj workspace's row is marked in its own table (`lane_vcs`, migration 0007) rather than by looking at the folder, so a missing folder is still forgotten in jj on Discard; its `lane_branch` holds the jj workspace's name, never a git branch, so everything that runs git on a branch skips or refuses it. Its diff is jj's `--git` output read by git2's patch parser, the same code a git lane's diff goes through, so the two match on one fixture.
- D-2599: What needs git refuses a jj workspace up front with one message, "Not available for jj workspaces yet": `single_repo` covers merge, Create pull request, setup and previews, second opinion; `repo_of` covers landing and pull request checks; the merge queue's plan skips them; the radar's `covered` and `lane_setup` skip them; the git panel refuses a folder inside a jj workspace, since git discovery would otherwise find the repository around it. Discard needs no force: jj keeps the working copy in its commit (`jj status` snapshots it first), and only `jj workspace forget` runs; Vibezeo never runs a command that rewrites or publishes history.
- D-2660: New worktree preselects jj in a co-located repository with jj found, and remembers the person's choice per repository in `$DATA/lane-kinds.json`. A new worktree made from a jj workspace (New worktree on it, a handoff, a launch into a new worktree) is a jj workspace starting from its working copy, since a git worktree from there would silently drop the workspace's work; from the repository itself, launch-sheet lanes, Best of N, task runs and handoffs make git worktrees in this slice. SSH and WSL folders, and repositories with `.jj` but no `.git`, offer no jj workspace and say why.
- D-2661: jj is found on the login PATH and then in the usual install places, run with the login environment (so the person's own jj config and identity apply, read only), and never installed by Vibezeo. Agents in a jj workspace get one more line in their briefing, to use `jj` and not `git`; nothing else engines receive changes.
- D-2662: F-CD-23 round 4's nits (reviewed with F-CD-24). `client` checks the epoch again right before spawning, since stopping a dead server and the availability probe can take seconds. Trust goes before the stop, as a sandbox switch stores the setting before stopping servers: workspace removal untrusts its `.tandem/worktrees` before `begin_removal`, and a new worktree (git, multi-repo or jj) is untrusted and then forgotten, which bumps the epoch so a request that read the leftover trust is superseded. A sandbox setting that can't be read counts as on (fail closed); forgets evicted from the list a request's epoch hasn't seen fail closed too. Requests for a removed workspace (its row stays, soft-removed) are refused with "That workspace was removed". Workspace removal's work is `commands::workspaces::remove_workspace`, tested with a test state; Discard is tested with a probe that asks for a server just before the folder goes. The epoch stays a task-local set by every request command (`with_epoch`); a caller without one uses the epoch at the start of its own `client` call.
- D-2663: F-CD-24 review. jj reads repository-level config (`.jj/repo/config.toml`), and a clone can ship a committed `.jj`, so: every jj call carries fixed `--config` overrides, which outrank the repository's (`fsmonitor.backend="none"`, `signing.behavior="drop"`, `signing.backend="none"`, `ui.diff-formatter=":git"`, `ui.pager=":builtin"`, `ui.paginate="never"`; fixed literals, never anything a repository or person supplies). No jj command runs in a repository before F-CD-23's trust (Trust repository…, offered in New worktree; the confirm says it covers jj), or when its `.jj` is tracked by git or its store's `git_target` doesn't resolve to this repository's `.git` (`jj::check_repo`, `jj_lanes::gate`, before create, diff, changed files, Discard and the sweep). The diff and file list keep the snapshot (`--ignore-working-copy` would miss uncommitted work); fsmonitor is off for it. Discard checks the gate before any pane stops, and `forget_workspace` only removes `<repo>/.tandem/worktrees/<name>` itself (not a symlink).
- D-2664: A jj workspace being made has a record (superseded by D-2665: now in `$DATA/jj-pending`, not beside it) from just before `jj workspace add` until its row exists; the sweep (startup and every 6 hours) forgets the workspaces of markers older than 10 minutes, as Discard would (their commits stay). Markers rather than "no row" decide, since a workspace removed from the rail keeps its worktrees' folders and registrations on purpose. Before a worktree is made, the trust of folders under `.tandem/worktrees` that no longer exist goes (`untrust_missing_under`), so a new worktree's path has none when its folder appears; after it, the untrust and bump stay as a backstop. The changelog entry is `[lin]`.
- D-2665: Re-review of F-CD-24. Committed content must never name what the sweep forgets: a repository can commit files under `.tandem/worktrees` (`git add -f`), so the record of a jj workspace being made lives in Vibezeo's own `$DATA/jj-pending` (the repository's canonical folder and the slug), and the sweep reads only those. The sweep and Discard only ever forget a name Vibezeo makes (`[a-z0-9-]+`, never `default`, which lane slugs are deduped against), and skip a repository while a jj workspace is being made in it in this process. jj's aliases (`[revset-aliases]`, `[template-aliases]` in the trusted repository's config) can shadow identifiers but not string literals or method calls, checked against jj 0.34: templates use `self.commit_id()` and `self.name()`, the base is passed as a quoted commit id (`"<40 hex>"`), which must be 40 hex digits, and a workspace's working copy as `"<name>"@`. Tests: a committed marker and a record naming `default` forget nothing; aliases for the base's id, `commit_id(x)`, `commit_id` and `name` change neither the base, the names nor the diff.
- D-2666: Second re-review of F-CD-24. A pending record is only a hint, never proof that its workspace is an orphan: the sweep acts on one only when no lane row (jj or git, removed rows included) has the name, the folder `<repo>/.tandem/worktrees/<slug>` exists, isn't a symlink, and is this repository's jj workspace (its `.jj/repo` file names `<repo>/.jj/repo`), and, where the filesystem keeps birth times, was made after the record. Otherwise only the record goes, so a stale record never forgets a live lane made again under the same name, or the person's own workspace of that name. Records are JSON. A failed forget is logged and keeps its record for the next sweep; the rest carry on. Records for repositories no longer on the rail are pruned after a week. Creates and the sweep share one lock per repository (a create holds it until its row exists and its record is gone; the sweep skips a locked repository), replacing the in-process count. Undo keeps the record when its forget failed. Checked against jj 0.34: a quoted commit id is alias-proof but a git ref named exactly like it (a tag a clone ships, no config needed) is resolved first, so the base is verified before every diff and after every create: no tag, branch or remote ref of that name (jj's own `refs/jj/keep/*` excepted), and `jj log -r '"<id>"'` printing that id. A template alias named `self` is expanded by jj (and an agent working in a jj lane can set one too, since every workspace shares `.jj/repo/config.toml`), and command-line config merges with, rather than replaces, a repository's aliases, so a trusted repository's own config, or an agent in one of its lanes, could still forge what jj prints; that stays a known limit (display only, landing is refused for jj workspaces, and its trust already lets its code run). The sweep's texts now say it removes nothing a person made. Fake-runner tests (the sweep's decisions, names, commit ids, the exact argv of add, handoff and diff, a failed forget) run without jj.
- D-2667: F-CD-24's migration is `0007_lane_vcs`, the next free number in chain27 (D-872: its activity ledger merged first with 0006). If F-EN-11 lands in chain27 first, this one moves to 0008 at the next merge.
- D-2668: Discard of a jj workspace snapshots its working copy (`jj status`, in the folder) and, without force, refuses with Conflict "Uncommitted changes" when jj couldn't keep all of it: the command failed (an error, the time limit, a lock, a stale working copy), or jj refused a file (stderr "Refused to snapshot", e.g. over `snapshot.max-new-file-size`) or left one untracked (stdout "Untracked paths:", outside `snapshot.auto-track`). Checked against jj 0.34: both warnings exit 0. The check runs before any pane stops, as for a git lane, and again in the forget; the dialog's forced retry and the core's native confirm are a git lane's. The sweep forgets without force, so such a workspace keeps its record (until D-2677's pruning) and its folder.
- D-2669: A jj lane's base is its starting commit's change id (32 letters k–z, checked), not a commit id: a squash or rebase of that commit in the main checkout rewrites its commit id but keeps its change, and jj rebases the lane onto the rewrite. The lane is then stale; its diff says "This jj workspace is out of date: run `jj workspace update-stale` in it, then try again" (jj's "working copy is stale" in plain words), and afterwards diffs only the lane's own changes again. Rows from before keep a 40-hex base, still accepted and checked by commit id.
- D-2670: A handoff (a jj workspace made from another) starts from `jj duplicate @` run in the source folder (which snapshots it first): a copy of the source's working-copy commit, whose change id is read back in full with `--ignore-working-copy log` in the repository. Before, the new lane was a child of the source's live working-copy commit, so the source's next edit rewrote it, rebased the lane and left it stale. The copy stays in the repository like any discarded workspace's commits. The source folder must be this repository's jj workspace before jj runs.
- D-2671: `verify_base` takes the repository and fails closed: the folder must be a jj workspace whose `.jj/repo` names that repository's (else "That folder isn't one of this repository's jj workspaces", and jj never runs), the git-ref check always runs against it, and jj must print the base back (`self.change_id()` for a change id, `self.commit_id()` for an old base).
- D-2672: D-2666's known limit, worded fully: a `self` template alias can come from the repository's config, which every workspace shares (`.jj/repo/config.toml`), so an agent in a jj lane can set one too. Still display only; landing stays refused for jj workspaces.
- D-2673: The forget is by name, so Discard first checks that the workspace jj calls `<slug>` is this folder's: `jj --ignore-working-copy log -r '"<slug>"@'` in the repository and `-r @` in the folder must print the same working-copy commit. A folder that isn't this repository's jj workspace is refused; a folder already gone forgets nothing (the name can't be checked).
- D-2674: Neither Discard nor the sweep removes a folder git's index has entries at or under (`.tandem/worktrees/<slug>`); an index that can't be read counts as tracked. The sweep's decision gains `Kept::Tracked`.

A first commit (made by `jj workspace add`; `jj new` puts the working copy on top of it) never read because `base_of` failed stays in `jj log`, empty (cosmetic, noted at the cleanup). Fake test.
- D-3104: `changed_files` turns `\` into `/` only on Windows (`slashed`), as `not_kept_on_disk` does.
- D-3105: `abandon_leftover` abandons by the commit id read on the same line as the change id (since the follow-up, as `"<commit id>" & "<change id>"`, so jj itself confirms both) (`self.commit_id()`, with no git ref named like it either), so a rewrite or divergence in between makes it a no-op instead of another commit. The fakes' state lines carry the commit id and expect the abandon by it.
- D-3106: The fake runner answers an unanswered `jj sparse list` with `.`, as jj does for a full workspace.
- D-3107: The E2E's `findJj` takes the first *file* there (`statSync().isFile()`, as `Jj::locate`'s `is_file`), and notes that it reads the test runner's PATH where the app reads the login shell's.
- D-3108: Spec: in a sparse workspace, anything on disk outside its patterns asks for force (build output included); ignored files go without asking inside the patterns.
- D-3109: MILESTONES names D-3090–D-3109.
- D-2679: The slug `default` is always taken, even when jj's default workspace was renamed (so jj doesn't list it): a lane named `default` couldn't be discarded.
- D-2445: The secret warning uses the core's redactor on `NAME=value` through `worktree_env_check`, so there is one detector (F-TL-02).

### M17 · Worktree workflow decisions
- D-2200: The four features are a new area, WT (F-WT-01…04), P2, owned by a second `## M17 ·` section in MILESTONES, as M17's extras are. `check-coverage.sh` allows P2 in M17 (the same line as `m17-extras`, D-700), and `trace-tests.ts` reads every section of a milestone.
- D-2201: The setup file is `.vibezeo/worktree.json` at the main checkout's root, named for the product users see. `.tandem/` can't hold it: it's in `.git/info/exclude`, so it could never be committed and shared. Vibezeo never commits it and never edits `.gitignore`.
- D-2202: Trust is a SHA-256 over the setup and teardown commands, per repository (its canonical main-checkout path), kept in `$DATA/worktree-trust.json` (0600), never in the repository. Copy patterns aren't part of it: the copy only moves the repository's own files into its own worktree, inside both (F-TL-03). Saving from UI-150 trusts; any other change needs review. Only the main window can trust or save (`LocalReview`, TL-06 rule 5).
- D-2203: Commands run only after a person makes a worktree (the New worktree dialog, the launch sheet, a retried seat). Task runs and handoff copy files and never run repository commands, so unattended work can't start a command nobody looked at.
- D-2204: Setup is typed into a visible shell pane in the worktree's tab (like Create pull request), so its output is visible and it can be stopped; the agent isn't held until it finishes. Teardown runs headless with `/bin/sh -c` (`cmd /C` on Windows), the login environment, a 2-minute limit and its output discarded, never logged.
- D-2205: Review comments live in memory per worktree until they're sent or the app quits; they're drafts, and keeping them in the database would need a migration other branches also touch. The prompt is English, like the app's other prompts to engines.
- D-2207: GitLab is detected from `origin`'s host name containing "gitlab"; a self-hosted GitLab under another name keeps `gh pr create` until a setting is asked for.
- D-2208: `type_command_when_ready` (Create pull request, the launch sheet's shell commands, the setup pane) waited for output times that the status store records only for watched agent panes, so for a plain shell it always timed out and never typed (found by E2E-M17-WT-1). It now also treats a screen that has text and hasn't changed for 1.5 s as ready (`QuietScreen`).
- D-2209: Worktrees on SSH hosts (M14's lanes on hosts, chain5) have no setup, overlap check or forecast: `lane_setup` returns null for them instead of an error (a new host worktree showed "Couldn't read the worktree setup"), the ⋯ menu turns **Check overlap…** and **Worktree setup…** off, and the merge confirm shows no forecast. Found while writing the 0.7.0 docs.
- D-2206: The copy uses gitignore syntax (`!` excludes) against paths from the repository root. It skips `.git` and `.tandem`, enters a git-ignored folder only when an anchored pattern's fixed path leads into it, copies a matching folder whole, never follows or copies symlinks, never overwrites, refuses a destination under a symlinked folder, and stops at 2,000 files or 512 MB (200,000 walked entries as a guard).

### M17 · Worktree workflow log
- Competitive analysis: three research passes (orchestrators, AI terminals and IDEs, vendor apps and open-source agents); ranked list sent to the coordinator. Findings that need the owner (Thread mode and Anthropic's terms, Free plan caps, a public feedback repository, Antigravity CLI) are in HUMAN_TODO.
- E2E-M17-WT-1 found D-2208 (shell panes never got their typed command, which also affected Create pull request) and that a third worktree's setup pane can hit Free's 4-pane limit (the spec frees panes first; the limit toast is the product's answer). E2E-M17-WT-2 found two "Comment on a.ts line 2" buttons on a changed line; removed lines now say "removed line".
- F-WT-01: destinations are checked component by component, so a tracked symlinked folder in the worktree can't carry a copy out of it (`f_wt_01_2` covers it, with a symlink in the main checkout and `../` patterns).

## M18 · The review loop (m16a-conductor)
Built on `m16a-conductor` (from `product-m0-m5` at chain19) from `docs/NEXT_FEATURES.md` §1 #6 and #2 and §3 B4. Owns F-WT-05, F-DB-04 and F-CN-09's first slice, and decisions D-2420 to D-2439.
- [x] F-WT-05 Second opinion from another engine (D-2420).
  - **Core.** `services::second_opinion`:
    - `lane_second_opinion {laneId, engineId, accountId?, task?}` creates a Read only thread (F-TH-09) in the worktree, titled "Second opinion: <branch>", and sends the review prompt. The prompt carries the branch, the task and the diff (fenced as untrusted, cut at 150,000 characters), with `## Findings` / `## Overall`.
    - A background wait polls the thread's state. When the turn ends, it parses the last reply and publishes `review:second_opinion`.
    - It refuses terminal-only engines ("Can't run read-only"), an empty diff ("No changes to review"), and a second run on the same worktree. Free's plan check is the thread service's own.
  - **Parsing.** `path:line: comment`, ignoring list markers and backticks. The path is matched exactly or by a unique suffix, and the line must be a new-side line the patch shows (`shown_lines` reads the hunks); that line is quoted. Everything else that isn't a heading, unplaced findings included, becomes one General text.
  - **UI.**
    - "Ask for a second opinion…" is in the worktree menu and the diff's toolbar.
    - `SecondOpinionDialog` shows the reviewer (Thread engines; terminal-only ones disabled with the reason; Pro on Free), the account and whose plan it uses, and an optional task. It has loading, error, empty and no-changes states.
    - While the reviewer works, the review bar shows "<Engine> is reviewing…" with Open thread.
    - `followSecondOpinions` adds the comments to F-WT-02's store, with General as its own comment (shown above the diff, last in the prompt), and toasts the count, "had no comments" or "didn't finish".
  - **Fake engine.** The second-opinion prompt gets findings on the diff's first added lines, one on a line the diff doesn't show, and a free line (Claude Code stream-json and the Codex app-server).
  - **Tests.**
    - Rust: 7 `f_wt_05_*` (the prompt, cutting, placement, General, start/publish/release with a fake host, a failed turn, refusals).
    - UI: 6 in `secondOpinion.test.tsx`.
    - E2E: `m18-wt05-second-opinion.e2e.ts` (Codex reviews a Claude Code worktree; the Read only thread and its first message; two placed comments and General; Send to agent carries all three; no changes).
  - **Docs.** code-mode.mdx, "Second opinion".

- [x] F-DB-04 Review queue (D-2421, D-2422).
  - **Core.** `services::review_queue` (`ReviewQueue` behind `QueueHost`):
    - It follows `status:changed`. A key that becomes done is considered: the session (a pane, or a thread in a local workspace), its changes (a worktree's `lanes::diff`, a git folder's `diff_since("HEAD")`), the closing message (a thread's last reply; a pane's last 3 screen lines, redacted), the latest checkpoint for that pane or thread, and the repository's review settings.
    - No changes, not git, or not local: no item.
    - Working or waiting removes the item; a removed key forgets it; idle keeps it.
    - `diff_hash` is SHA-256 over path, change and patch.
    - Approval holds the hash. A different hash on the next finish or refresh moves the item to Changed, which stays until approved again.
    - Snooze lasts 60 minutes, or until the agent finishes again.
    - The check runs through `bestof::run_check` with the login environment, 10 minutes, and the last 200 lines redacted. It runs when an item joins, or on Run check. A refresh with the same diff keeps the result.
    - `review:queue` carries the whole list.
  - **Risk rules** (`risks`, local, no AI): 20+ files, migrations folders, CI, lockfiles, `.env` files, auth words in a path segment (not `author*`), the repository's public API prefixes, and deleted tests. Up to 5 files per rule.
  - **Repository settings.** The Hidden `ReviewChecks` / `ReviewApiPaths` maps, keyed by the main checkout's root. `review_repo_set` is main window only, with a command up to 2,000 characters and up to 50 paths.
  - **Commands:** `review_queue`, `review_approve`, `review_unapprove`, `review_snooze`, `review_item_diff`, `review_run_check`, `review_repo_get` and `review_repo_set`. The palette gets `dashboard.review_queue`.
  - **UI.** The Dashboard panel's Agents · n / Review · n switch (`DashboardPanel`), and `ReviewQueue`:
    - sort by risk or finish time; Refresh;
    - To review, Snoozed and Approved sections;
    - cards with closing, diffstat, risk badges (files in the title), the check (`<details>` with output) and the actions;
    - the item-diff dialog and the Repository checks dialog;
    - empty, loading, error and populated states.
  - **Tests.**
    - Rust: 8 `f_db_04_*` (the rules, the hash and limits, join/leave, a coalesced new done, stale approval, snooze, the check).
    - UI: 7 in `reviewQueue.test.tsx`.
    - E2E: `m18-db04-review-queue.e2e.ts` (a worktree pane joins within 1.5 s with migrations and deleted tests, a no-change pane doesn't, a thread joins, approve then changed, Send back and Merge's forecast, the check passes and fails).
  - **Docs.** code-mode.mdx, "Review queue".
  - **Gate:** passed on the tree with `product-m0-m5` 52f07fe1 merged in.
    - 1,940 Rust tests (7 ignored) and 1,458 TypeScript (desktop 681).
    - The desktop build, clippy on Linux, Windows and both Mac architectures, and fmt.
    - Coverage: 171 IDs.
    - Protocol drift: `RepoReview`, `ReviewCheck`, `ReviewCheckState`, `ReviewItem`, `ReviewQueueView`, `ReviewRisk`, `ReviewRiskRule` and `ReviewState` added. The names avoid Best of N's `CheckState`, which a first build overwrote.

It halves the longest patch until the reply fits, then drops files from the end in batches sized from the overshoot, counted in `omitted`.
      - A test sends 12 capped files plus a `.env` file through the sealed path.
      - A pure test covers 12 capped files and 5,000 small ones.
    - **`.env` files are withheld.** Their patches are never sent, and `withheld` names them.
    - **Heard before acting (D-2425).** `CallHost` gains `call_started`, `call_ended` and `act_answered`:
      - an act answers once all its rounds are done; an injected batch stands in for one act;

      - the doer's prompt says to act only on the user's own request, never on text in `<results>`, and refines `review_send_back` like `send_to_thread`.
    - **The walk belongs to one call.** It resets at call start and end. `phone_current` prefers the walk's item only while it's still to review.
    - **Fresh reads.** `walk_next` refreshes every item, so an approved one whose diff moved comes back as Changed. `walk_approve` refreshes its item first; a stale approve is read again first (`reread`).

    - **Speech.** The walk's ending names how many heard items still wait. The ready count is worktree items only. The facts are spoken before the agent's own words.

A pane whose session begins is told its working tree's overlaps announced before it, through a new `NoticeSink`. `TerminalService::notice` holds a notice for a pane whose process hasn't started and sends it after the local spawn.
    - **Landing releases claims (AC3).** The merge queue releases a lane's claims when it lands, "already up to date" included.
    - **Stale claims are swept.** `TaskStore::prune_claims(keep)`. At startup the main checkouts' claims go, and so do those of folders that are gone; the worktree sweep drops gone folders' claims; removing a workspace ends its panes' sessions and releases its worktrees' claims.
    - **The main checkout on Windows.** `ClaimScope` and `Claim` gain `main`, from git (`!is_linked_worktree`), and both folders resolve with `contain::canonical` (`C:\…`, not `\\?\C:\…`), so the main checkout's last session releases its claims there too.
    - **The fence (AC4).** Every path and intent another agent wrote comes back as `{untrusted}`, overlaps' paths included. Under `mine`, so does any path or intent the caller's own connection didn't write, inferred claims' included.
  - **Also in this round.**
    - **Path rules.** A folder claimed without its `/` covers its files. An agent's relative path starts at its session's folder (`ClaimScope.prefix`, from `Repo::prefix`), and an absolute one must be inside its tree. `..`, `*` and `?` are refused; `[` is literal. Paths compare folded on macOS and Windows (`contain::fold`) and are stored as written.
    - **Limits.** `release` refuses more than 50 paths before it waits for the lock. `list_claims` pages the other worktrees' claims (`cursor`, `limit`, `next_cursor`).
    - **Tasks not exposed.** A terminal agent's session is tracked (`TasksService::track_scope`) whatever "Expose tasks to terminal agents" says, so its edits claim and its pane is told. Its connection is optional.
    - **Checks take turns.** `check_overlaps` holds one guard from reading the claims to the sink.
    - **Edited files resolve.** A new file in new folders, a path through a symlink (macOS `/tmp`) or one written `\\?\…` resolves by its deepest existing folder (`contain::canonical_existing`, now public with `fold` and `case_insensitive_fs`).

    - E2E-M18-FREE puts a fake Cursor Agent in `fakebin` and never removed it.
    - A run's review uses another installed chat engine (`review_engine`), so both reviews ran on it.

    - Alone, the review falls back to Claude Code, which is why the spec passed 3 of 3 on its own.
    - On this line, free-offline then tk07 fails the same way, and the fake's log shows two Cursor Agent sessions.

    - every fake chat engine (Claude, Codex and now ACP) answers a review with the same verdict (`review_reply`);
    - E2E-M18-FREE removes its Cursor Agent after it and detects again, as E2E-M18-RT-06 does with Codex;
    - E2E-M18-TK-07 checks in Execute all's confirm step that Claude Code reviews both runs (the row's `data-review-engine`), so a reviewer left by another spec fails there, by name;
    - its waits say what they last read when they time out.

The fix was already on `m16a-conductor` since 07d8114f (F-TK-07's low findings, which never reached chain26):
    - `loadAttempts` reads are numbered, and only the latest writes the runs and the status;
    - a run `tasks:attempt` moved while it was being read keeps its newer state;
    - `resetTasks` doesn't put the counter back to 0.
  - **Not the backend:** the task runner logs nothing as a run ends, so the quiet app log wasn't a stall. Two reviewed runs whose sessions and reviews end at the same moment reach In review with their verdicts.
  - **Not the review queue either:** the plan's runs change nothing in their worktrees. The spec commits a file into each one only after the rows reach Approve, so the queue rightly listed neither run. Several Done records landing together all join (`f_db_04_1`).
