### M18 · Next features: engines decisions
- D-2400: Each engine's instructions files and pointer are data in `registry.json`, checked against the vendors' own pages on 15 October 2026: Claude Code's memory page (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`; `AGENTS.md` only when none exist; `@path` imports), Codex's AGENTS.md page (`AGENTS.override.md`, else `AGENTS.md`, one per folder), Gemini CLI's GEMINI.md page (`@file.md` imports; `context.fileName`), Copilot CLI's custom instructions page (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, combined) and Cursor's CLI page (`.cursor/rules`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`). Every pointer is an `@AGENTS.md` import in the engine's own file: Gemini CLI takes one in `GEMINI.md`, so its settings file is never edited, and no engine needs a symbolic link. Engines without an entry (Grok, OpenCode, Droid, Amp, Aider, Kimi) are Unknown until their docs are checked.
- D-2401: F-EN-07 is P2, in a new milestone section, M18, which `check-coverage.sh` accepts for P2 next to M16 and M17. The panel opens from a local folder's rail menu only: a palette command would need a folder context in E2E-M3-9, and the menu is where Worktree setup already is.
- D-2402: "Use one file for all" replaces a file's text only after a confirmed plan whose digest (each path, its text before and after) still matches. Each replaced file is copied to `$DATA/instructions-backup/<change>/` with a manifest first, and Undo puts every file back byte for byte, or removes the files the change created, only while each still holds what the change wrote. Without `AGENTS.md`, the user picks the file it starts from (`CLAUDE.md` first). A file whose text isn't in `AGENTS.md` is marked "Its text will be replaced".
- D-2403: "Copy into worktrees" writes only `.vibezeo/worktree.json`'s `copy`, through `tandem_git::setup`, never `worktree_setup_save`: that one trusts the file's commands, and adding a copy pattern mustn't trust commands nobody reviewed. Trust is a digest of the commands alone (D-2202), so it stays as it was.

- D-2404: Antigravity CLI and Kiro CLI are added only with what their vendors' own pages say (15 October 2026): antigravity.google/docs/cli/install (`agy`, the scripts for macOS, Linux and Windows, browser sign-in with the token in the keyring, no home variable) and /docs/cli/gcli-migration (reads `GEMINI.md` and `AGENTS.md`); kiro.dev/cli (one install command for macOS, Linux and Windows, used verbatim for all three), /docs/reference/cli-commands (`login`, `logout`, `whoami`, `KIRO_HOME`) and /docs/reference/settings. Antigravity keeps one account per computer (`homeStrategy: none`): its keyring entry would be shared. Ready and waiting patterns stay empty until a signed-in run records them (HUMAN_TODO), as Amp's are; limits use the common patterns. Neither gets a `headlessCmd`, a chat adapter or a status command: Kiro's `whoami` exit code isn't documented, and Antigravity's terms for automation wait on the owner. Gemini CLI's note follows Google's 19 May 2026 post: paid API keys and Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise keep it, personal accounts moved to Antigravity CLI on 18 June 2026. The site's "11 engines" copy describes the shipped download and changes with the release that carries these rows.
- D-2405: "Models listed from the CLIs" means the Thread engines' pickers, which already lead with what the engine reports (Codex's `model/list`, ACP's `session/new`) before the catalog (F-TH-08); F-EN-09.4 pins that. Terminal engines have no model picker, and Kiro's CLI has no `--model` flag, so `kiro-cli chat --list-models` isn't read.
- D-2406: An engine's install method comes from where its command leads after following links: a `node_modules` folder is npm, a Homebrew `Cellar` or `Caskroom` is Homebrew, the engine's own versions folder in the user's home (Claude Code's `~/.local/share/claude/versions`) is its own installer, and anything else is "installed another way". Nothing is asked of the engine or a package manager to find out.
- D-2407: Pin is only the engine's own documented switch, added at launch: `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` for Claude Code (its settings page) and `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false` for Codex (its config reference). Vibezeo never edits an engine's settings files, and panes already open keep running as they were. Engines without a documented switch show "no documented way" instead of Pin.
- D-2408: "Last good" is the version that last finished a Thread turn without an error; a turn the user stopped or one that hit a usage limit counts for neither. The thread service calls a health sink at every turn end, and the banner shows only when the current version differs from the last good one and a turn failed since. Terminal panes don't report results, so they never mark a version.
- D-2409: Running in the background lists this user's processes (effective uid) with no controlling terminal, outside the app's process tree, whose executable is an installed engine's command, or a runtime (`node`, `bun`) whose first argument is the engine's script; wrappers aren't the engine. The table comes from `sysinfo` (exact argv, so paths with spaces match), the terminal from `/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux and `ps -axo pid=,tty=` on macOS; Windows has no listing yet. A row shows the engine's name, and its subcommand only when it's one the engine documents (Codex's `app-server`, `exec`, `mcp`…; Claude Code's `mcp`, `update`…): any other word after the command may be a prompt or a key. Stop sends SIGTERM (`kill -TERM`) after a confirm, from the main window, and only to a process still listed with the same pid, engine and start time (D-2500). Codex's own daemon settings aren't documented, so the list is generic.
- D-2410: Check for updates runs `npm view <package> version` in the login environment, only when clicked and only for an npm install; nothing checks on a timer. For other methods it shows the command that updates the engine (`brew upgrade`, `claude update`). A rollback command is shown first in the Install sheet and runs only in a visible pane.
- D-2411: The library opens only the engines' session files, by layout: Claude Code's `projects/<folder>/*.jsonl` and Codex's `sessions/` up to five folders deep, `*.jsonl` only. It never follows a link (`O_NOFOLLOW` on Unix, and links aren't listed), so a credential file next to them (`.credentials.json`, `auth.json`) is never opened; F-TH-17 AC5's test records every open through the `SessionFs` fake. A file with no line that parses, or no session id that's safe as an argument, is skipped and counted. OpenCode's storage isn't read yet: its format isn't documented.
- D-2412: Each engine's own home is read as one more source with no account, after the accounts: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` from the login environment when absolute, else `~/.claude` and `~/.codex`. A home already read for an account isn't read twice. Resuming one runs the engine as the user does in a terminal: the pane has no account, the launch sets no provider-home variable (with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, Claude Code reads `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json` and, on macOS, a Keychain entry keyed by that folder, so the session could come up signed out), and no status hooks are written into the user's own home. `LaunchConfig.own_home` marks such a relaunch; every other relaunch still needs its exact home (review of 16 October).
- D-2413: Resume reuses F-SH-07's resume path instead of a new launch: `library_resume` writes the pane's session row (the engine's session id, the session's home as its launch configuration) and marks the pane, and the pane's first start runs as Resume. The session opens in the deepest open local workspace containing its folder, else in its repository (the git root, else the folder) added as a workspace under the plan's limit. Sessions on SSH hosts or in WSL aren't listed.
- D-2414: Search is the one Pro part (NEXT_FEATURES §4, owner's call pending): the API grants `sessionSearch` with Pro and Team through the shared `LIMITS`, and an older API's entitlement parses as off. The index holds prompt and reply text as storage, never logged or sent; it lives in its own file so turning search off deletes it whole, and Delete all removes it with `$DATA`. The Privacy switch goes through `library_search_set`, not `settings_set`, so turning it on checks the plan.
- D-2415: "Continue with another engine" writes the brief from the transcript with §6.11's fallback (the last 200 lines, redacted) instead of asking an engine: the source session isn't running, and a headless run would spend a turn the user didn't ask for. The sheet offers the session's folder only; no worktree, thread or "close the original".
- D-2416: Session text goes through the global redactor (`Redactor::global()`, F-TL-03's patterns and registered secrets) as the library parses it, so a title, the transcript view, the Continue brief and `session-index.db` never hold a token a user pasted into a session. The engine's own file is untouched; the library just never copies a secret out of it (CLAUDE.md: secrets live only in the keychain). The test searches a session by its other words and checks the token is in none of the index's files.
- D-2500 (review of F-EN-08, 16 October): Stop's identity is the pid, the engine and the process's start time from the OS. The list sends the start time; Stop lists again and refuses unless all three still match, so a process that exited and whose pid went to another engine process isn't signalled. A pidfd would close the remaining gap between the check and the signal on Linux only; with the start time the gap is a few milliseconds, so it isn't used.
- D-2501: Only a Thread turn on this computer moves "last good", and only the engine's own failure counts against a version: an error event with stage Spawn, or the code `engine_exited` (its process died mid-turn), `ErrorStage::engine_fault`. An engine's generic error result (Claude Code's non-success `subtype`, Codex's unclassified `turn_failed`, ACP's `prompt_failed`), being offline, signed out, a model the account can't use, a tool's own failure, a stop or a usage limit record nothing: the engine answered, so it works. The thread service remembers whether a turn had an engine fault and checks the thread's workspace is local (or none) before calling the health sink (re-review, 18 October).
- D-2502: Install and Roll back from Settings and the thread banner open their pane in a local workspace's tab: the active tab when it's local, else the first local workspace's, else none, and the sheet then offers Copy only. Detection, which rechecks the result, reads this computer.
- D-2503: A Pin may not set any engine's provider-home variable, `HOME`, `PATH`, `SHELL`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_PATH`, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `ZDOTDIR`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*` or `TANDEM_*` (registry validation), and its environment is set before the provider home and the status hook, which win. Version regexes keep a pre-release suffix (`0.47.0-alpha.3`). npm's `node_modules` under Bun's, Yarn's or pnpm's global folders is "installed another way" (no npm rollback), the home is canonicalized before it's compared with the engine's own versions folder, and `npm view` runs in the data folder so a project's `.npmrc` can't steer it.
- D-2504 (review of F-TH-17): The index is format version 2 (`PRAGMA user_version`): any other version is deleted and built again, so an index from before redaction doesn't keep a token. `secure_delete` is on, so deleted rows are overwritten. Turning search off through any path (the switch, `settings_set`, `settings_reset`, Conductor's `set_setting`) deletes it, and `settings_set` refuses turning it on without Pro. A search re-checks the setting after indexing and deletes the index if it was turned off meanwhile. Index writes take one lock and a 5 s busy timeout, and the UI gives listing and the first search 2 minutes.
- D-2505: The library's reads are bounded: a file is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, must be a regular file of at most 64 MB after opening, and is read through a 64 MB limit. A line is read at most 4 MB at a time and a longer one is skipped to its newline without being held. A transcript keeps its last 2,000 turns. `projects/` and `sessions/` must be real folders, not links; the home itself may be a link. A listing serves the commands that follow it for 30 s instead of every command reading every home again.
- D-2506 (F-EN-10, 18 October): Built-in ACP modes come from each vendor's own page: Gemini CLI's ACP page names `gemini --acp` (`--experimental-acp` is the older flag), Kiro's names `kiro-cli acp`, goose's names `goose acp`. Gemini CLI becomes a Thread engine; Kiro stays terminal-only because F-EN-09 AC3 decided so for both new engines, pending the owner; goose isn't in the registry, so it's the form's preset. Free still runs Claude Code and Codex in threads only (`chatEngines`), so every ACP engine, added or built in, is Pro there.
- D-2507: Test sends `initialize` and nothing else: no `session/new`, so the agent never opens a session, reads a folder or runs a tool before it's added. It runs in the user's home with the login environment plus the form's variables, and is killed after the answer or after 10 s. A line that isn't JSON, a request instead of an answer, an error answer or another protocol version is "Not an ACP agent" with the reason. Add runs the same test, so a saved agent always answered once.
- D-2508: An agent signs in its own way, so Vibezeo holds none of its credentials (CLAUDE.md): a variable value or an argument the redactor sees as a secret is refused with "Keep keys in the agent's own sign-in", and so are names a Pin may not set (D-2503) and any `*_BASE_URL`. Agents that need a key read it from their own config or sign-in.
- D-2509: Added agents are kept in `$DATA/acp-agents.json`, not in settings: setting maps hold strings, booleans and string lists only. The command is resolved to an absolute path when added (on the login PATH unless it's already absolute) and that path is what threads run; detection doesn't look for it, and a missing path lists it as not installed. An added agent's registry entry carries vendor "ACP agent", which is how `EngineView.added` is set. Added agents run on this computer only.
- D-2510 (the coordinator's call, 20 October): Kiro CLI is a built-in Thread engine through its documented `kiro-cli acp`, which supersedes F-EN-09 AC3's first version ("neither new engine appears as a Thread engine"). F-EN-09 held both new engines back for the same reason, Antigravity's unsettled automation terms; Kiro documents ACP for clients like this one, so that reason never applied to it. Its threads run in the account's provider home (`KIRO_HOME`), like its panes, and were Pro, as every engine beyond Claude Code and Codex, until D-869 made every chat engine free. Like every engine with a chat adapter, it's offered as a teammate engine too. Antigravity stays terminal-only and is never run headless; Kiro isn't run headless either. Its registry note says it runs through ACP.
- D-2511 (review of F-EN-10): An added agent's id is `acp-`, a slug of its label and 8 random hex digits, unique among the registry's ids, so an id isn't given again after Remove: an old thread can't run a later agent that took the same label. An added agent's adapter is built from its saved settings each time a thread starts (the startup adapters cover bundled and remote engines only), and those settings meet the form's rules again on every read of the file and before a thread runs. Remove ends the agent's live sessions, stopping a running turn first; its threads stay and their next turn says the agent was removed. Add and Remove hold one lock across read, change and atomic write.
- D-2512: An added agent runs the absolute path saved when it was added, or nothing: no detection result and no PATH lookup stand in for it, so a missing program never becomes another program of the same name.
- D-2513: Hosts (SSH and WSL detection and their engine lists), engine versions and their background-process check, instructions, usage and the launch sheet's terminal engines use the registry without added agents: an added agent is a Thread engine on this computer only.
- D-2514: A sign-in error from an ACP agent names the methods it gave in `initialize`, as it named them (control characters removed, at most 8). For an added agent, Sign in shows how to sign in with its own command in a terminal: Vibezeo has no account or provider home for it, so it never opens an account's login.
- D-2515: Allow once picks the agent's `allow_once` option only; when the agent offers none, the request is answered `cancelled`, never with `allow_always`. Allow for this thread still falls back to `allow_once`, which grants less.
- D-2516: Gemini CLI's registry entry has `acpFallbackCmd: ["gemini", "--experimental-acp"]` (D-2506's older flag). When `acpCmd` starts no session for a reason other than a sign-in, the adapter starts the fallback once. The fallback runs the same program; the registry refuses one that doesn't.
- D-2517 (F-EN-11, 25 October): The finder asks this computer only. URLs are built from a port and a path with the host fixed at `127.0.0.1`, and the client refuses any other URL, uses no proxy (a proxy would carry the request off the machine), follows no redirects, waits 1 s and reads at most 4 MB. A typed host must be `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`; anything else, `::1` and `0.0.0.0` included, is refused before anything is saved. It asks only when Settings › Engines opens or on Check again, never on a timer. Added ports (up to 16) are the `local_model_ports` setting, `{"ports": ["kind:port"]}`, since setting maps hold strings and string lists; an added port takes the place of the default with its number. URLs are parsed: plain HTTP, host `127.0.0.1`, a port, no user information. An answer is read in chunks and dropped past 4 MB, or when its length says so. Start is off on Windows for now: PowerShell, `cmd` and Git Bash run their startup files before the command and there's no wrapper yet, so `local_models_list` gives `startReason` "Local models run on Linux and macOS for now" and Start refuses. A local pane's Codex is pointed only at the server, and runs with no proxy: its command is wrapped in `/usr/bin/env -u` each proxy variable, with `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy` set to both login values plus `127.0.0.1,localhost,::1` and `CODEX_HOME` set to the home. Set inside the command, these come after the login shell's startup files, which could otherwise export a proxy, a `NO_PROXY` without loopback, or another `CODEX_HOME`. Its `config.toml` sets `check_for_update_on_startup = false`. Ollama's cloud models (`remote_host`, `remote_model` or a `cloud` tag) are served through 127.0.0.1 but run on ollama.com, so they aren't listed. Ollama added as another kind lists them in `/v1/models` with nothing to mark them, so a server of another kind that answers is also asked Ollama's `/api/version` and `/api/tags` at once (up to 1 s more, 2 s per server): models the tags mark remote are dropped, and when the version answers but the tags don't, nothing is listed, since which models run elsewhere can't be known (fifth review). What the server does with a prompt (a gateway or a port-forward on that port could pass it on) and settings an administrator manages for Codex are outside Vibezeo's control: the Privacy line and the docs say so, rather than that nothing leaves the computer. A project's MCP servers and hooks were on that list until the seventh review: a local pane's Codex loads none of the repository's settings now (D-3065).
- D-2518: Start is Codex only, and only for Ollama and LM Studio: both servers document Codex through the Responses API (`wire_api = "responses"`), so that's what the `vibezeo-local` provider sets. llama.cpp's server is listed with its models but has no Start until Codex's support for it is confirmed. No other engine is offered: Claude Code and the ACP engines don't document a local OpenAI-style provider.
- D-2519: A local model's Codex runs in its own provider home, one per server and model (`$PROVIDERS/codex/local-<kind>-<port>-<model>-<hash>/`, kinds named as in IPC), with no account, so the user's `~/.codex` and Codex accounts are never touched and no sign-in is asked. The pane keeps its `LaunchConfig` (that home; the server and model; and of the user's Codex arguments only an allowlist, sandbox and approval flags and `-c` keys `approval_policy`, `sandbox_*` and `model_reasoning_*`, in every spelling Codex parses) in `panes.launch_config`, and each start writes the home's provider settings again before Codex runs, and every start of it, Normal, Fresh or Resume, in this run of the app or a later one, relaunches with it and no account. If the home is gone it refuses with "Launch configuration unavailable" and never falls back to an account. Only a folder on this computer can start one. Every start also passes the model, the `vibezeo-local` provider and its settings (name, `base_url`, `wire_api`) and `check_for_update_on_startup=false` as `-c` overrides, last, after `resume <id>`, a pin's arguments and the user's (D-3061), with the review and memory models and sub-agents off (D-3063), approvals to the user and nothing Codex fetches or sends itself (D-3067), and the pane's folders untrusted with `--cd` (D-3065): from Codex 0.149.0 (D-3062, D-3066) command-line overrides sit above every configuration file and no remote endpoint adds thread settings over them, and the repository's own `.codex/config.toml` isn't loaded at all, so it can't send a local pane's prompts to a cloud model (settings an administrator manages still can, and the docs say so). The variables that would sign Codex in or run its work elsewhere are unset with the proxy variables (D-3068). Each start first asks the server again: one that isn't running, or that no longer offers the model as one running on this computer (a name re-pointed with `ollama cp` to a cloud model), refuses with a message naming the server and model, and Codex doesn't start (fifth review). The check is per start: a name re-pointed while the pane runs is caught at its next start. The status hook is installed there as for any home, and `config.toml` keeps it. The pane's "{model} · {kind}" is a new nullable `panes.local_model` column (migration 0008, after the activity ledger's 0006 and F-CD-24's 0007: D-872), shown as the chip "On this computer" where the account chip would be. The Privacy page states it in a line under "What leaves this machine" rather than as a row: that table is `hosted-features.json`, the list of what does leave, shared with the website.
- D-3060 (F-EN-11, sixth review, 28 October): A local pane's safety from a project's own Codex settings rests on a list of keys (D-3063), and each Codex release can add a key that picks a model on the session's provider. A relay on 127.0.0.1 that forwards to the server only the model Vibezeo checked would close the whole class; it's a follow-up, not this round. The seventh review closes it for the repository's own settings, which a local pane's Codex doesn't load (D-3065); the keys stay pinned for the layers that remain, `/etc/codex/config.toml` among them.
- D-3061: A local pane's `-c` settings go last on Codex's command line, after `resume <id>`, a pin's arguments and the user's. The last `-c` for a key wins in every Codex, and before 0.164.0, when both the top level and a subcommand had `-c`, Codex kept only the subcommand's: with the pin's `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false` after `resume`, every override before `resume` was dropped.
- D-3062: Local models need Codex 0.149.0 or newer (D-3066; the sixth review's 0.129.0 wasn't enough, corrected in the seventh). From 0.129.0 a project's `.codex/config.toml` can't set `profile`, `profiles`, `model_provider` or `model_providers`, and `-c` sits above every configuration file but an administrator's; in 0.128.0 a project's profile outranks `-c`, so it could name any provider. Start and every local start run `codex --version` on the program they would launch (5 s) and refuse below the floor, for a pre-release of it, or when no `codex-cli <version>` can be read, saying so with the version needed. `local_models_list` reads it the same way at each call (D-3069), so the page says it before a click.
- D-3063: A local pane sets every model key that reaches the session's provider to its model: `model`, `review_model` (`/review` uses it unchecked) and `memories.extract_model` and `memories.consolidation_model` (memories run on the session's provider). Sub-agents are off, since a sub-agent can name its own model, `agents.default_subagent_model` or a role's configuration file: `features.multi_agent=false`, `features.multi_agent_v2=false`, `features.enable_fanout=false` and `agents.enabled=false`, where a model's catalog entry can turn them on otherwise. Every Codex a local pane runs has `agents.enabled` (it came in 0.145.0; before it an unknown key under `[agents]` was read as a role, so the sixth review sent it only from 0.145.0, and the seventh always, D-3066). `experimental_realtime_ws_model` isn't set: realtime does use the session's provider (`prepare_realtime_start` takes `sess.provider()`, so its socket would go to the local server), but it needs API-key auth (the provider's key or bearer token, an account's key, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` for OpenAI's own provider only), which a local pane doesn't have, so it doesn't start. Corrected in the seventh review: the sixth said realtime didn't use the session's provider, and that analytics need an account; the analytics events do, but Codex's usage metrics go to ab.chatgpt.com without one (D-3067).
- D-3064: In the Ollama check of a server of another kind, a tags answer without a `models` list is no answer: with Ollama's version it lists nothing, without it the server's list stands.
- D-3065 (F-EN-11, seventh review, 28 October): A local pane's Codex loads none of the repository's own settings. At every start Vibezeo marks `trust_level = "untrusted"` for the pane's folder and each folder above it, each as given and with symlinks resolved, and for a linked worktree its main checkout (the `.git` file's `gitdir` three levels up, as written and resolved). They're written into the home's `config.toml`, where folders listed before (another pane's on the same model, or one Codex trusted) stay listed and become untrusted, and passed as one `-c projects={…}`, since Codex splits a `-c` key at every `.` and trust is read from the system, user and `-c` layers merged: nothing written to the shared home during the session changes it, and only an administrator's managed config outranks it. Codex starts with `--cd <folder>`, so a login profile's `cd` can't move it to an unmarked folder. From Codex's source, 0.149.0 and main: (a) a project layer that isn't trusted is disabled; the effective config, hooks discovery, exec policies and MCP servers read enabled layers only, the hook-state and skill-rule readers take only user and session-flag layers, and the rest show warnings or copy layers with their disabled state; project skills and `AGENTS.md` still load as instructions. (b) 0.149.0 to 0.155.0 show the trust screen only when trust is unset; 0.160.0 to main show an untrusted folder as "Open restricted", which writes nothing; the app server trusts a folder only when its trust is unset. (c) A folder is looked up by its canonical and given keys, from the start folder up to the project root, then the project root and a linked worktree's main checkout. In an untrusted folder Codex's default approval policy is `untrusted` (it asks before every command and edit) with the workspace sandbox; the user's own `-a` or `approval_policy` still sets it.
- D-3066: The floor is Codex 0.149.0, and a pre-release of it is refused. From 0.129.0 to 0.148.x `experimental_thread_config_endpoint` can load a thread's settings from a remote endpoint, inserted above the command line's; 0.149.0 has no such key, and its `experimental_thread_store_endpoint` is a removed key that only fails a start. Codex 0.149.0 retired `--full-auto`, `-a untrusted` and `-a on-failure`, so a local pane keeps only `-a on-request|never`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` and its other allowlisted arguments.
- D-3067: A local pane turns off what Codex would fetch or send by itself and the other ways a model or a reviewer could be chosen for it: `features.enable_fanout=false` (on 0.129.0 to 0.144 an enabled fan-out turned multi-agent back on; from 0.145.0 it's a removed key), `approvals_reviewer="user"` (never a reviewing sub-agent), `features.apps=false` (the hosted connectors), `features.plugins=false` (with no account offering a remote catalog, Codex syncs its curated plugins from `github.com/openai/plugins`, the GitHub API or a chatgpt.com archive at startup), and `analytics.enabled=false` (Codex's usage metrics go to `ab.chatgpt.com` by default, without an account).
- D-3068: A local pane's command unsets every variable Codex 0.149.0 signs in with or runs its work elsewhere by: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (a personal access token or agent identity), `OPENAI_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` and `OPENAI_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_CONTEXT` (workload identity), `CODEX_CONNECTORS_TOKEN` (the connectors' bearer token), and `CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_URL` with `CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_NOISE_REGISTRY_URL`, `…_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `…_AUTH_TOKEN` and `…_CHATGPT_ACCOUNT_ID`, which run its commands and file reads on another machine.
- D-3069: The Codex version a local pane checks is the word after `codex-cli ` at the start of a line of `codex --version`'s output (stdout, then stderr), so another program's version there (a package manager's notice) is never read as Codex's. `local_models_list` resolves the program Start would run and reads its version at each call, rather than the version detected when the app started, so Check again on the page shows the Codex installed now; not installed, the page says to install it as before.
- D-3070 (F-EN-11, follow-up, 29 October): `write_config` takes a lock per home (a map from the home's path to its mutex) across reading, changing and writing `config.toml`, so two panes on one model starting at once can't drop each other's folders: each start's write keeps every folder listed. Writes to different homes don't wait on each other. D-3073 extends it to Vibezeo's other two writers of the file.
- D-3071: A Codex version's build metadata (`+…`) is ignored when it's compared, as in semver: `0.149.0+build` is 0.149.0. The part before `+` decides, so `0.149.0-alpha.1+build` is still a pre-release and refused.
- D-3072: A home's `projects` list keeps every folder a pane on that model has started in, all untrusted, and isn't pruned: an entry costs a few bytes, and dropping one could only let a folder go back to unset trust. The docs and PRODUCT_SPEC say so.
- D-3073 (F-EN-11, second follow-up, 29 October): One lock per home, `tandem_engines::homes::config_lock` (a map from the home's path to its mutex), is held across each of Vibezeo's reads, changes and writes of Codex's `config.toml` there: `write_config` (the local model's settings and folders), `install_hooks` (the status hook) and `set_stdio_server` (the tasks server). D-3070 locked only the first, so a start's hook or tasks-server write could put back a file it had read before another start's folders were written, and lose them, or lose the hook's line. All three are synchronous, so a std `Mutex` is enough, and none is held across an await. Codex itself may still rewrite the file, and no lock inside Vibezeo covers that; each pane's own `-c projects` already governs its session.
- D-3074: The Codex version Start's reason names ("this computer has Codex …") is shown without control characters, as server and model names are, and cut at 40 characters with "…".

## M16 mobile-apps checklist (LAN pairing, Vibezeo Remote, push, Linux stores)
Built on branch `mobile-apps` (from `m16c-phone-companion`, with `product-m0-m5` merged). Owns F-RM-04 LAN pairing, F-RM-05 Vibezeo Remote app, F-RM-06 Encrypted push and F-RM-07 Linux store packages (new spec entries, PRODUCT_SPEC §4.14; MILESTONES M16 owns them). Decisions are D-2000–D-2099.
- [x] F-RM-04 LAN pairing.
  - **Desktop relay.** `services::phone_lan`: `LanServer` binds one socket per private IPv4 address (RFC 1918 as `lan`, 100.64.0.0/10 as `vpn`), never `0.0.0.0`, loopback, a public address or IPv6, and re-scans every 30 s. `accept_one` closes connections from outside the LAN unread; `serve_connection` reads the request head itself (httparse), refuses a `Host` that isn't the socket's IP (421), and either upgrades `/v1/relay/:pairing_id` (tokio-tungstenite on the raw stream, 64 KB limit) or serves the phone web app. `LanHub` is the relay's pairing table with F-BE-11's semantics (D-2003); the desktop's end is in-process (`attach_desktop` gives the same `RelayLink` the hosted relay socket does), so `PhoneService` didn't change beyond `pair_begin_via(PairVia::Lan)` and the `PhoneNet::{create_lan_pairing, forget_local}` defaults. `LanNet` makes a random 32-byte token per pairing and keeps only its SHA-256 (keychain `NS.remote / lan:<pid>`), restoring it after a restart.
  - **Commands.** `phone_pair_begin {via: "lan", address?}` (no account or plan; org policy still applies), `phone_lan_state`, `phone_lan_set {enabled, port?}` (main window). ARCHITECTURE §3, §13.3 and §16.1 (threat 16).
  - **UI.** Settings › Remote › Local network: the switch (off), where it listens, the address the code uses (LAN or VPN), "Pair a phone on this network", the port error, and the Tailscale note; the pairing dialog says the phone must be on the same network.
  - **Phone web app on the LAN.** `apps/web/remote-lan` builds the same `RemoteApp` with Vite into `resources/remote-web` (`sh scripts/build-remote-web.sh`; not committed). Served at `http://<ip>:<port>/remote` with a CSP whose `connect-src` is that one `ws://` socket. Without WebCrypto (not a secure context) the IndexedDB store seals with XChaCha20 instead (D-2004).
  - **Shared code (D-2008).** `apps/web/lib/remote/*` moved to `packages/remote` (`@tandem/remote`), with `session.ts` (the screen logic: phase, connection, snapshot, notices, `relayAllowed`, `linkFromUrl`) and `demo.ts` (a simulated computer speaking the real protocol).
  - **Tests.** Rust: 15 `phone_lan` (F-RM-04.1–.5 over real sockets on loopback with the real `PhoneService`: pairing and a command, replay, 1008/1003/1009/4000, revoke, restart, the web app and rebinding, a non-LAN peer, turning it off) and `invariant_rule_7_lan_mode_is_off_by_default_and_never_public`. TypeScript: 3 Settings › Remote (F-RM-04), the LAN store without `subtle`, `relayAllowed` and a refused internet `ws://` code (F-RM-04.6).
- [x] F-RM-05 Vibezeo Remote app (`apps/mobile`, Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86).
  - **Screens.** Welcome (scan, paste a link, Try the demo; pairing, failed and unpaired states), the camera scanner (expo-camera), and Home: Agents (status, Type to this agent with Terminal control), Approvals (Allow/Deny, a queued allow says it waits at the computer, the step-up note), Threads and teammate chats (paged transcript, send with Chat control), Routines (Run now), Settings (computer, connection, the phone's grants, notifications, push, Unpair with a confirm). Tablets and wide screens get two columns (list beside the open thread or agent). Every list has empty, loading, error and populated states. Strings live in `lib/strings.ts`; colours, radius and spacing in `ui/tokens.ts`, checked against `packages/ui`'s tokens.css.
  - **Logic.** `packages/remote/src/session.ts` (`RemoteSession`) holds the screen logic for both the app and tests; `linkFromUrl` reads the desktop's web link, a LAN link and `vibezeo-remote://pair#p=…`; `relayAllowed` refuses `ws://` to anything but private, VPN or loopback IPv4 (D-2006). The pairing is in the Keychain / Keystore (`lib/secureStore.ts`, expo-secure-store, `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`), split into parts with a two-generation pointer so an interrupted save keeps the previous pairing (D-2010). `lib/runtime.ts` gives Hermes `crypto.getRandomValues` (expo-crypto) and a UTF-8 `TextDecoder` (D-2011).
  - **Demo mode.** `packages/remote/src/demo.ts`: a made-up computer inside the app that speaks the real protocol over an in-memory socket, labelled on every screen; "Simulate activity" finishes an agent and raises an approval (D-2012).
  - **Notifications.** New approvals and agents that finish, need you or fail become an in-app banner while the app is open, or an OS notification while it's in the background (`lib/notify.ts`), once each; never sent anywhere.
  - **Native config.** `app.config.ts`: `com.vibezeo.remote` on both platforms; camera permission (no microphone); `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` and Android cleartext for LAN mode (D-2013); the `vibezeo-remote` scheme and App Links / Universal Links for `app.vibezeo.com/remote` (D-2026); the privacy manifest (no data collected, no tracking, the required-reason APIs; D-2024); `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = true` (D-2025); target and compile SDK 36, min SDK 24, iOS 16.4. `plugins/withReleaseSigning.js` signs release builds with the owner's upload key from outside the repo; `eas.json` builds and submits both stores.
  - **Android build (done here).** `bash scripts/mobile/build-android.sh` runs `expo prebuild` and Gradle and writes `dist/mobile/VibezeoRemote-<version>.apk` and `.aab` with SHA256SUMS, refusing a debug-signed result, and checks 16 KB alignment (`zipalign -P 16`) and the AAB's signature. This container's build was signed with a throwaway key (HUMAN_TODO). Maven Central answers 429 through the agent proxy, so `~/.gradle/init.d/central-mirror.gradle` points Gradle at Google's mirror (container setup, not repo).
  - **iOS (prebuild done here).** `expo prebuild --platform ios` writes the project with the push extension target, the shared keychain group, the privacy manifest and associated domains. Compiling needs a Mac or EAS (HUMAN_TODO has the steps).
  - **Store.** `apps/mobile/store/LISTING.md` (true claims only, review notes for the demo, privacy answers), `PLAY_CLOSED_TEST.md`, and `scripts/mobile/screenshots.mjs`, which renders demo-mode previews with react-native-web in Chromium (no emulator here: no KVM).
  - **Tests.** Mobile (Vitest): 19: secure store (round trip in keystore-sized parts, interrupted save, clear), runtime polyfills, notifications and prefs, strings, tokens against tokens.css, the signing plugin, the push extension plugin against Expo's template project, push on the phone. `packages/remote`: session and demo (11), push vectors.
- [x] F-RM-06 Encrypted push.
  - **Format (D-2021).** `tandem_core::remote::push` and `packages/remote/src/push.ts`: ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439, so CryptoKit opens it), `0x03 ‖ 0x01 ‖ seq ‖ nonce ‖ ct`, AAD binding the pairing and sequence; pinned by `tests/fixtures/remote_push_v1.json` (the Rust bytes matched the TypeScript ones on the first run).
  - **Desktop.** Phone commands `push.register {platform, token, key}` (hosted pairings only) and `push.unregister`; the registration lives in the keychain and goes on revoke or a 410. `PhoneService::push_alerts` (after each coalesced bus burst) seals new approvals and agent changes for phones that registered and aren't connected, saving the sequence number before sending, through `PhoneNet::push` → `POST /v1/pairings/:id/push`.
  - **API.** `POST /v1/pairings/:id/push`: the caller's live pairing, Pro, 60 a minute; forwards and stores nothing; logs pairing, platform and outcome only; imports no crypto. Providers: `FcmPush` (HTTP v1, service-account JWT), `ApnsPush` (HTTP/2, ES256 provider token, generic alert + `mutable-content`), `MockPush`; `PUSH_PROVIDER=live` picks each platform by its credentials.
  - **Phone.** `lib/push.ts`: turning Push on (Settings, off by default) makes a fresh key, stores it with the pairing id in the keychain (`AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`, shared group on iOS), gets the device token and registers; off unregisters. Android opens data messages in a background task; iOS's Notification Service Extension (`plugins/ios-push-extension`, Swift + CryptoKit) does it before display.
  - **Tests.** Rust: 2 vectors, 4 phone-service push tests (nothing until registered; sealed and opened only with the key, sequence 1, 2; unregister, revoke and a dead token stop it; bad registrations refused). API: 4 route tests (forwarding, no payload or token in logs, ownership, revoke, 410, size), 2 provider tests (APNs against a local HTTP/2 server with a verified ES256 token; FCM's message). Mobile: opening alerts, replay, wrong pairing.
  - **Unverified here:** the Swift extension has never been compiled (no Mac), FCM and APNs have never been called for real (no accounts). HUMAN_TODO.
- [x] F-RM-07 Linux store packages (as far as this container allows).
  - **Flatpak.** `packaging/flatpak/com.vibezeo.Vibezeo.yml` repackages the release .deb on GNOME 51 with Flathub's libappindicator shared module and git built in; `com.vibezeo.Vibezeo.metainfo.xml` validates with `appstreamcli` (pedantic: only the uppercase id note); a desktop file and launcher. Built here with flatpak-builder from 0.5.0's .deb and run under Xvfb: the welcome screen came up inside the sandbox. GNOME 48 is end-of-life, which the first build showed, so the manifest uses 51.
  - **Host commands (D-2032).** `tandem_core::sandbox`: inside a Flatpak, terminal panes (`tandem-pty`), threads (`tandem-engines` chat process), login-env capture and engine detection start through `flatpak-spawn --host --watch-bus --directory=… --clear-env --env=…`, with exactly the environment they'd get outside. Nothing changes outside a Flatpak. Not yet exercised inside a real Flatpak (0.5.0 predates it); HUMAN_TODO has the check.
  - **Snap.** `packaging/snap/snapcraft.yaml`: classic confinement (D-2031), core24, from the release .deb with its libraries staged and patchelf. Not built (no snapd in the container).
  - **Tests.** `f_rm_07_3_host_commands_carry_their_folder_and_exact_environment`.

### mobile-apps decisions
- D-2000: Phones get **Vibezeo Remote**, a native companion, built with **Expo / React Native** in `apps/mobile`: the owner-approved exception to DECISIONS' Tauri-only stack (the desktop stays Tauri 2). Phones can't run the coding CLIs (iOS forbids spawning processes; Google Play forbids downloaded executables), so the phone app is the F-RM-03 companion. PRODUCT_SPEC §6 items 3 (no native apps) and 8 (no store distribution) are superseded for the phone companion and the Linux stores by the owner's direction.
- D-2001: LAN mode is the free path: the desktop is its own relay on the local network. It needs no account, plan or hosted service, so it isn't Pro-gated (the hosted relay stays Pro, F-RM-03); a Team's `disablePhone` still turns it off. Remote access away from home is a VPN (Tailscale's free plan), documented, not built.
- D-2002: LAN mode listens per private IPv4 address only, never `0.0.0.0`, loopback, public addresses or IPv6 (home networks hand phones IPv4; telling ULA from global IPv6 with privacy addresses isn't worth it yet). Peers outside private, VPN, link-local and loopback ranges are closed unread, and `Host` must be the socket's IP literal.
- D-2003: The LAN relay keeps F-BE-11's wire behaviour (subprotocol token, 1008 after upgrade, 1003, 1009, 4000, `peer` notices, 50 frames/s with a burst of 50). The rate limit counts phone frames only: the desktop end is in-process. Tokens last until revoke, as D-1904; the 10-minute QR lifetime is still the one-time secret `S`.
- D-2004: The desktop serves the phone web app itself on the LAN, because a page from an HTTPS origin can't open a `ws://` socket (mixed content). It's the same `RemoteApp`, built by Vite (`apps/web/remote-lan`) into `resources/remote-web`. Plain HTTP on a LAN address isn't a secure context: no service worker (Add to Home Screen still works) and no `crypto.subtle`, so the pairing in IndexedDB is sealed with XChaCha20 under a random key kept beside it. That's D-1909's residual risk without the non-extractable key; the origin serves only this page.
- D-2005: Turning LAN mode on is `phone_lan_set` (main window, `LocalReview`), kept in `$DATA/remote/lan.json`, not a settings key: `settings_set` has no window check, and opening a listening socket is a choice made at the desktop. Default port 47800.
- D-2006: The phone apps follow a `ws://` relay only to private, VPN, link-local or loopback IPv4 addresses (`relayAllowed`); `wss://` anywhere. A crafted code can't point a phone at a plain-text server on the internet (the frames would still be sealed).
- D-2007: `PhoneThread` gains `teammate`, and the phone's thread list includes teammate chats, which F-RM-03's Chat control covers ("send to threads and teammate chats").
- D-2008: The phone's shared TypeScript lives in `packages/remote` (`@tandem/remote`): protocol, client, stores, the session controller and the demo computer. The web PWA, the LAN web app, desktop E2E, web E2E and Vibezeo Remote import it; nothing is copied.
- D-2009: `commands::phone::start` starts the phone service in every build (it returned early without hosted endpoints), because LAN pairings exist without them.
- D-2010: Vibezeo Remote keeps the pairing in expo-secure-store (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore-backed), readable only while unlocked and never backed up. Values are split into 1,800-character parts behind a generation pointer, so a crash mid-save leaves the old pairing.
- D-2011: The app uses the same audited @noble libraries as the web app (one implementation, checked against the shared vectors) rather than a native crypto module. Hermes gets a CSPRNG from expo-crypto and a UTF-8 decoder polyfill where missing.
- D-2012: Demo mode is a simulated computer that speaks the real protocol, so App Review and curious users exercise every screen without a desktop; it is labelled on every screen and reaches no network (`demo: true` allows only the demo relay).
- D-2013: Android allows cleartext and iOS `NSAllowsLocalNetworking`, for LAN mode's `ws://`. The app's own `relayAllowed` limits plain `ws://` to private and VPN addresses (D-2006), and every frame is end-to-end encrypted either way.
- D-2014: The Android release is signed by `plugins/withReleaseSigning.js` from Gradle properties the build script reads from `~/.vibezeo/android` (outside the repo); a release signed with the debug key is refused. The key made in this container is throwaway: updates must be signed with the owner's key, so nothing built here is for publishing.
- D-2015: Screens are React Native components drawn with `ui/tokens.ts` (packages/ui's values, test-checked); packages/ui's DOM components can't run in React Native.
- D-2020: Push is opt-in per phone, needs a hosted-relay pairing (LAN mode has no server to push from), and the API is a stateless forwarder: the desktop sends the phone's token with each alert, so the API stores no tokens.
- D-2021: Push alerts use ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) with a per-registration random key the phone makes, not the session's XChaCha20 keys, so iOS's CryptoKit can open them in an extension without the session state, and a rekey never strands an alert. A sequence number (saved before sending) lets the phone drop replays.
- D-2022: iOS gets a generic visible alert ("Vibezeo · Something on your computer needs you.") with `mutable-content` and the sealed bytes; the Notification Service Extension replaces the text after opening it with the key from the shared keychain group. If it can't, the generic text shows: no readable content ever passes through the API or Apple.
- D-2023: The desktop pushes only to phones that aren't connected, and only on new approvals and on agents turning waiting, done (from working) or failed, with redacted, clipped text.
- D-2024: The privacy manifest declares no collected data and no tracking, plus the required-reason APIs the Expo and React Native modules use (UserDefaults CA92.1, file timestamps C617.1, boot time 35F9.1, disk space E174.1).
- D-2025: `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = true`: the app's own encryption is standard but beyond Apple's exempt categories. The owner files the self-classification report (HUMAN_TODO).
- D-2026: Universal Links and App Links cover `https://app.vibezeo.com/remote*`; the portal serves `apple-app-site-association` and `assetlinks.json` from `APPLE_TEAM_ID` and `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256` and answers 404 until they're set.
- D-2030: The Flathub id is `com.vibezeo.Vibezeo` (the desktop bundle id is `com.vibezeo.tandem`, which store ids would freeze; Flathub wants the product name last). The Flatpak repackages the signed release .deb rather than building from source, since the source repository is private.
- D-2031: The Snap uses classic confinement: Vibezeo starts the person's own shells and coding CLIs in their folders, which strict confinement forbids. That needs the Snap Store's manual approval.
- D-2032: Inside a Flatpak, everything that runs the person's tools runs on the host through `flatpak-spawn --host` with an explicit environment (terminals, threads, the login env, engine detection); git is bundled in the sandbox instead. Environment values pass as `--env=` arguments, so a same-user process can read them from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` as it already can from `/proc/<pid>/environ` (ARCHITECTURE §16.1's residual risk).
- D-2040: In a build without Vibezeo accounts (`TANDEM_HOSTED=0`, D-833), Settings › Remote keeps the Pro callout for the hosted relay only, worded "Pairing through the Vibezeo relay is part of Pro … pair over your local network below", never asks to sign in, and offers the Local network section in full: F-RM-04 needs no account, plan or hosted service (D-2001). The 8-hour arm switch shows only with a paired phone (D-833), which a LAN pairing can be.

### mobile-apps log
- F-RM-04: the LAN relay, its commands and UI, the LAN web app, `packages/remote`. The 15 Rust LAN tests passed on the first run; clippy wanted `from_phone` renamed (`from_*` takes no `self`). The UI test found `Callout` doesn't pass `data-testid` through. The first LAN web app build linted as source: its output is now ignored by ESLint.

- F-RM-05/06: the Expo app, demo mode, push end to end, the iOS extension, store files. What the runs found: Expo SDK 57 needs iOS 16.4 at least (prebuild refused 15.1); Gradle's Maven Central downloads got 429 through the proxy (Google's mirror fixed it); the release JS bundle needs `babel-preset-expo` declared in a pnpm workspace; the first push tests failed because a phone that just sent a frame counts as connected (the tests now disconnect it, as a closed app does); the LAN hub could close a revoked phone before the desktop's `bye` reached it (the close now queues behind the desktop's frames, through a weak sender so a dropped link still ends); merging `product-m0-m5` duplicated a `tandem-store` line in `tests/invariants/Cargo.toml`.
- F-RM-07: the Flatpak (built and started here), the Snap YAML and host commands in a Flatpak. A full gate run caught the LAN revoke race again under load: once the desktop's link is gone, the weak sender can't carry the end marker, so the forwarding task now finishes a revoked slot itself when its queue closes. Four full desktop test runs after the fix: 528/528 each.
- Android release built here: `VibezeoRemote-0.1.0.apk` (73 MB, arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64) and `.aab` (49 MB), 16 KB aligned, signed with a throwaway upload key.

## Design direction (`design-lead`)
The owner (20 October): the product and the site should feel premium, "not something cheap and just another product", so people stay, try it, use it and pay; "the features are primary but the look and feel is equally important". Branch `design-lead` (from `product-m0-m5`) sets the direction for both surfaces in `docs/DESIGN.md`, builds the shared token layer and reviews the two implementing sessions' work: `app-ui` (D-2600 on) and `site-motion` (D-1870 on). Decisions D-1890 to D-1899, then D-2700 on (the coordinating session, 20 October): D-1870 to D-1889 are the website session's and D-1900 on the phone companion's.

### Design direction decisions
- D-1890: `docs/DESIGN.md` is the design direction for the app and the site: five brand attributes (calm, precise, fast, trustworthy, crafted; when they conflict, trustworthy > fast > calm > precise > crafted), principles from the design books, what makes premium products feel premium, the shared system, the journey from first visit to paying with concrete changes and owners, and how a READY is reviewed (must-fix or polish). It starts from an audit of vibezeo.com 0.8.0 and its live demo at 1440×900 (§0): the product starts below the fold, the home page is 12,984 px, teal does six jobs, the demo opens on an empty thread under a six-step coach card, and the app's surfaces don't share the site's light and depth.
- D-1891: one token source. `packages/ui/src/styles/brand.css` (new) holds the brand layer both surfaces use: edges, fills, elevation e1–e3, the rings' light, card and frame radii, the expo-out curve. `site.css` keeps its `--site-*` names as aliases and mirrors the light block under `prefers-color-scheme`, as D-1801 does for `tokens.css`. The app imports it but changes nothing until a slice uses it. Migration slices T1–T7 are in DESIGN §4.1.
- D-1892: one accent, three jobs: the primary action, focus and selection, and a control's active state. On the site at most three teal elements per viewport (eyebrows, inline links and ticks go neutral); in the app one accent-filled button per view. Status colours stay status only, each with its shape.
- D-1893: the path to paying is honest by rule (DESIGN §5.5): no plan prompt during first run; a limit is explained at the control that hit it, free way out first; Pro lists only what `LIMITS` gives it and the download runs, with hosted features apart under "Comes with accounts"; buttons that can't work today say "Tell me when accounts open"; no countdowns or repeated nags. Two lines in 0.8.0 break it and are on `app-ui`'s list: "Unlimited panes & threads" and "upgrade for unlimited panes" (Pro is 64 panes, 6 threads).

- D-1894: the neutrals are `ink`, a true neutral near-black, for the app and the site; slate leaves every semantic token. `app-ui` built it in its slice 1 (D-2600) from the coordinating session's first brief, which predates DESIGN.md, and the coordinating session asked the design lead to choose between ink and slate. Compared at 1:1 in the demo and on the site, slate's blue cast washed teal and the status colours toward one cool tint; every premium dark product measured grounds on a neutral near-black (#08090A, #07080A, #0D0E11), a convention rather than anyone's signature. Kept from DECISIONS: 6 px controls (the site's buttons and the nesting depend on them); adopted from D-2600: 10 px panels, panes, cards and popovers, so a 6 px control nests in 4 px of padding. One elevation set: `brand.css`'s `--tn-edge-hi` and `--tn-elev-1…3`, with the app's `--shadow-1…3` as aliases. DESIGN §4.2, §4.5, §4.7 and the T8 slice (the site on ink) follow. DECISIONS' visual identity is amended in `app-ui`'s branch, worded as this decision.

- D-1895: engine marks are our own monograms on small tinted tiles, after `app-ui` and the coordinating session raised telling engines apart at a glance in a grid of four or more panes. The letterform carries identity and the tint is a quiet second cue: low-chroma OKLCH tokens in `brand.css` (`--tn-engine-<id>`, dark and light, for the app and the site), letters in `fg`, hues chosen away from each vendor's brand colour and checked against the vendor's site before shipping, never a vendor logo, colour or gradient. The status bar follows the coordinating session's call: quiet by default, items only while non-zero, at most four, waiting first (DESIGN §4.6, §5.4.6).

- D-1896: with Vibezeo free (D-869), the journey's last step is no longer paying. DESIGN §5.5 becomes "the moments that make someone stay, tell a friend and come back": the first agent working (first run under a minute, the first finish as the peak), the first worktree landed (Best of N and the review queue get the craft budget after the Dashboard; we earn the recommendation and never ask for it inside the work, with no share prompts, referral codes or tracking), and coming back to exactly where you left off. Rules: no plan UI anywhere once the release that lifts the limits ships (until then a limit is stated as a fact of that version, with no way to pay past it); free said once, plainly, where it answers a question. Hosted features carry one phrase, "Comes with Vibezeo accounts", as the 0.9.0 docs already say, always with "It uses Vibezeo's servers and switches on when Vibezeo accounts open." (or that sentence as its tooltip), and the action "Tell me when accounts open"; never Pro, premium, paid, upgrade, plan, trial, credits, a price or a date. DESIGN §9 retires the plan and limit strings (§9.5 lists the keys) and keeps the voice rules.

- D-1897: the home page's length target is ≤ 8,000 px at 1440 (it was 6,500): the hero scene and the product scenes replaced screenshots and earn their space. `site-motion`'s 0.10.0 merge (10,153 px) ships first; the next site slice cuts the Land scene (to the changelog or the worktree docs), the principles row (to /about/), the engines section's old capture, and 32 px of desktop section spacing (DESIGN §5.1.4).

- D-1898: product scenes on version pages (`site-motion`'s chain27 slice, REMAINING §0.2). Each scene sits full width directly above its own Added card, never stacked before the notes: Land already does, as 0.9.0's first card. The order is the 0.12.0 plan, 0.9.0's CI results, 0.11.0's claims and 0.11.0's resource governor, which is the first to drop. Scenes show a worktree by its name (`checkout-fix`) where the app shows its branch (`tandem/checkout-fix`), as the Land scene does, under the caption's "simplified"; the site never shows the placeholder prefix, which is a question for the owner. Lighthouse CI adds `/changelog/0.12.0/`, and `/changelog/0.9.0/` with its second scene. The home page is unchanged.

- D-1899: the demo catches up with the releases (`app-ui`'s 0.13.0 slice 2, REMAINING §0.2, D-868). The order is one sample world shared with the scenes, then Land worktrees, the intent radar, CI results, and the smaller features after. The opening frame moves into that world on a frame the app can reach: an agent launched into a worktree gets the worktree's own workspace and tab (`launch.rs`), and Code mode shows one at a time, so worktree agents never share a grid. It opens on `coupon-rules` with Codex at work, with `checkout-fix` (Done) and `search-ui` (Waiting, hint 1) in the rail under `shop`; the still and both alts that describe the frame change with it. Every addition follows these rules: only states the app can reach (a check passes only after a push; Execute stays refused); one source for the sample world's names, which the scenes and the demo both read; a first frame as calm as today, with the coach's three hints; Reset restores everything; data from the outside world is labelled as a sample in the data.

- D-2700: rail marks (the radar mark, D-2613; the checks badge, D-2614) show a short form that fits, never a phrase cut off: the checks badge uses the status bar's own words ("CI failed", "CI running", "CI passed"), and the radar mark is its icon and the symbol (`applyCoupon`, or "3 symbols"). A long symbol may be cut at its end; a state or a verb never is. Beside a row's status, or when even the short form doesn't fit, a mark is its icon alone. The full sentence ("1 check failed: test", "Shares applyCoupon") is always its accessible name and tooltip. Marks stay on the row's one line.
- D-2701: a rail row never runs past the rail. While a row overflows, it folds in this order: the radar mark to its icon, then the checks badge, then the status words to their dot, each keeping its words as accessible name and tooltip (D-2700). The name keeps its 10-character floor. The rail's minimum width is the measured width of a fully folded row at the deepest indent (the name's floor, its dot, the marks' icons and the pane count), likely about 230 px where it was 180; the collapsed rail stays for anyone who wants every pixel for panes. A mark's accessible name begins with its visible words (WCAG 2.5.3): "CI failed: 1 check failed: test".
- D-2702: the hero is one Code-mode window as the app lays it out, with one worktree in view (D-1899). It is `site-motion`'s next slice, before 0.11.0's Claims. The window:
  - the rail;
  - Code mode on `checkout-fix`'s tab, with Ada's pane alone, since each worktree's tab holds its own agent;
  - the sidebar's Dashboard tab on Review. Ada's card arrives there when she finishes ("Review · 0" and "Nothing to review", then "Review · 1"). It no longer floats over the grid, because finished work goes to the queue, not to a toast.

  The rail is drawn as 0.12.0's WorkspaceSlot and WorktreeRow draw it: each worktree's branch icon, its name, its slot ("● 1 working"; `search-ui` turns to "Needs you" in amber at 2.2 s), the radar mark inline and the count badge, with the rail wide enough that nothing is cut. The radar notice and "Warned both agents" are toasts at the bottom right, and the status bar carries the agents segment ("◆ 1 waiting ● 1 working"). At 390, the rail's worktree rows sit as a strip above the pane, so the agent that needs you shows on a phone, and the sidebar floats over the pane as the app's does below 1,100 px. Caption: "Three agents work in one repository, each in its own worktree, and the rail shows the one that needs you." At release, a "scenes to 0.13.0" slice moves every scene's rail to D-2611, D-2613, D-2700 and D-2701, and the Dashboard to F-TL-12.12, gated on 0.13.0 as LANDS is gated on 0.9.0.
- D-2703: the rail's minimum (D-2701) counts F-CD-24's jj badge and the Preview's globe only while a row in the rail shows them (`app-ui`'s option 2). Most people keep 246 px; a jj repository with a running preview gets up to 297. A rail sitting at its minimum widens when such a row appears, eased over `--dur-base` with `--ease-standard` and never mid-drag. It doesn't narrow by itself when those marks go, since its width stays until someone drags it, so panes reflow once, not twice. A fixed 297 would cost everyone 51 px for a rare row, and leaving 246 would let that row run past the rail.

### Design direction log
- Read the brief's sources, captured vibezeo.com and its live demo (Playwright, Chromium, 1440×900, dark and light), inventoried the journey as built (welcome, five-step wizard, launch grid, empty states, every upgrade prompt and its copy, raw colours and arbitrary values) and studied premium product sites for principles only.
- `docs/DESIGN.md` written (D-1890 to D-1893).
- T1, the shared token layer (D-1891): `packages/ui/src/styles/brand.css` with the edges, fills, glow, rings, highlight ink and elevation e1–e3 (dark and light), `shadow-e1…e3`, `rounded-card`, `rounded-frame` and `ease-out-expo`. `site.css` aliases its `--site-*` names to them, mirrors the light block as its section 1b, and no longer defines the shadows, radii or curve itself; the app and the site import `brand.css` after `tokens.css`. No component changed. `site.test.ts` checks the new mirror, and that every themed site token either has a light value or aliases a brand token that has one. Checked unchanged: `build:site` on this branch and on `product-m0-m5` (ea582544), served side by side, give identical computed styles (box shadow, background, radius, colours, easing, size) on every element of eight pages and the demo app, in dark and light; ten of twelve full-page captures are pixel-identical, and the home page in light differs between two captures of the same base build too.
- The gate on T1: lint; TypeScript 1,564 tests (ui 412, desktop 747, api 225, web 116, remote 33, mobile 21, protocol 10); Rust 2,147; the desktop build; clippy on Linux, Windows and macOS; fmt; no protocol drift. The fresh container first needed `pnpm infra:up` (images through `mirror.gcr.io`) and `scripts/bootstrap-linux.sh` (`libdbus-1-dev` and the rest).
- Design QA of `site-motion` slice 1 (dark mode, 73b6a6b5), sent to the coordinating session: not yet.
